Photo by Aizar Raldes / AFP via Getty Images. Thursday, October 1, 2026 -** Iran : Iranian President says Tehran will pursue U.S. dialogue. Tehran rejects report U.S. ordered its UN delegation to leave New York. UK says there are "strong indications" Iran played role in RAF Fairford incident. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims six militants killed in southeastern Iran. Yemen : Saudi-backed forces, Ansarallah report strikes in Taiz and Saada. Palestine : Israeli attacks continue as 105 bodies recovered from Gaza City rubble are buried. Israeli strike kills Palestinian journalist in Gaza, bringing journalist death toll to 263. Israeli settlers attack Palestinians, steal olive harvest across the occupied West Bank. Lebanon : Israeli attacks continue across south Lebanon despite U.S.-brokered agreement. Lebanon documents suspected Israeli war crimes. Syria and Hezbollah hold first known face-to-face talks in Turkey. U.S. : U.S. economy grew 2.2% in Q2, upgraded from earlier estimate. Tennessee botches second execution this year, governor halts all remaining 2026 executions. War Secretary Pete Hegseth announces new drone command, 20 percent cut to generals in "State of the Force" speech. Federal Trade Commission launches investigation into OpenAI, Anthropic over AI safety. ICE briefly published, then removed, internal reports showing medical failures in 33 detainee deaths. Department of Justice files ethics complaint against nearly all Minnesota federal judges over immigration-surge comments. Senate confirms Keith Sonderling as Labor Secretary. Sen. Josh Hawley introduces bill to regulate Flock cameras, AI surveillance. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick reports over $250 million in income from 2025. Judge rules U.S. can deport Milwaukee Muslim leader on national security grounds. South Africa summons U.S. Ambassador for third time over "undiplomatic conduct." French court sentences 13 to prison over 2021 Channel crossing that killed 31 migrants. International : Bolivian attorney general detained days after U.S. revoked his visa over alleged drug trafficking ties. Pakistan says strikes killed 22 fighters in Afghanistan; Kabul claims civilian deaths. Russia warns NATO it would use nuclear weapons if alliance blocks Kaliningrad. Brazil briefs French, German officials on alleged U.S. and Russian election interference. Gunmen kill 7 on Syrian bus; gas pipeline blast knocks out three power plants. Iraqi armed group suspends military operations after U.S. troop withdrawal. China builds new military facility in Laos, possibly first full People's Liberation Army base in Southeast Asia. Norway's parliament probes Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre, 10 others over links to Jeffrey Epstein. Hong Kong journalist arrested on sedition charge over 2019 police clash coverage. MI5 warns UK academics to sever ties with Chinese research group over alleged spying. Rwanda open to hosting EU migrant transfer facilities, lawmakers say. Entire newsroom arrested in Egypt in significant press crackdown. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Iranian President says Tehran will pursue U.S. dialogue: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran would continue pursuing dialogue with the United States despite repeated attacks during negotiations. "We have never avoided dialogue and will not do so, although the United States targeted our country three times," Pezeshkian said, adding that Iran was also seeking to expand land-based trade with Pakistan, Iraq, Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan amid "restrictions at sea." Separately, President Donald Trump Time that Iran had made an offer concerning reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but said what he had seen was "simply not enough." Trump said renewed U.S. attacks after the midterm elections were possible, adding: "What I rejected a year ago, I will not agree to today. Iran could be destroyed, and that's possible." Tehran rejects report U.S. ordered its UN delegation to leave New York: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and the Iranian delegation New York on Monday evening according to a prearranged schedule that had been communicated to the U.S. State Department on September 17, Iran's UN mission said. The statement came after Axios, citing a source, reported that the U.S. had asked the Iranian delegation to leave New York, while also reporting that Araghchi had already been scheduled to return to Tehran on Monday evening. Iran's mission called the claim "baseless and worthless." UK says there are "strong indications" Iran played role in RAF Fairford incident: The government Iran played a role in an incident at RAF Fairford that led to the arrest of five UK nationals, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, but provided no further details or evidence for the claim. Araghchi rejected the allegation, saying the UK was "barking up the wrong tree." The five men, aged between 23 and 25, were arrested Sunday after police were alerted to three suspicious vehicles near the base. Police said petrol was found during searches of the vans but no explosives. All five were later released on bail. RAF Fairford has been used by U.S. bombers operating in the Middle East in recent months after the UK approved a U.S. request to use the base for strikes on Iran. IRGC claims six militants killed in southeastern Iran: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Thursday its forces killed six people in an operation against a group it alleged was planning an attack in the southeastern province of Sistan and Baluchestan. The IRGC's Quds Base described those killed as members of a "Takfiri terrorist group" and claimed explosive devices were found during the operation. Yemen Saudi-backed forces, Ansarallah report strikes in Taiz and Saada: Taiz, southwestern Yemen: Saudi-backed forces carried out six airstrikes on Ansarallah positions in Al-Akboosh and on fronts in Haifan district, the government forces said. Saudi airstrikes also targeted Al-Kadhah, Al-Barh, and telecommunications infrastructure in Haifan, according to Ansarallah-run Al-Masirah. Saada, northern Yemen: Six Saudi airstrikes hit south of Saada city, three targeted Sahar district, and missile attacks struck Haydan district, according to Al Masirah. Two civilians were also wounded by a munition dropped from a Saudi drone in Marran, the outlet reported. Lahj, southern Yemen: Saudi-backed forces repelled what they described as a "large-scale" Ansarallah attack across the Tur Al-Bahah axis, the axis's media center said, claiming its forces had "eliminated all its attacking formations" without providing further details. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, eight Palestinians were killed and 26 injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,040 killed, with 175,168 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,439 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,052, while 834 bodies have been recovered. Israeli attacks continue as 105 bodies recovered from Gaza City rubble are buried: Several Palestinians were on Thursday when an Israeli drone targeted Al-Mawasi in Khan Younis, WAFA reported. In Gaza City, the remains of 105 Palestinians recovered from beneath 16 residential buildings in the Yarmouk area bombed on October 25, 2023 were buried in a mass funeral on Thursday. The recovered bodies included 37 children and 38 women. More than 8,000 bodies remain beneath rubble across the Strip, according to Gaza's Civil Defense. Israeli strike kills Palestinian journalist in Gaza, bringing journalist death toll to 263: Palestinian journalist Mohammed Abdul Aziz al-Najjar was Wednesday in an Israeli strike on his hometown of Khuza'a, east of Khan Younis, according to Gaza's Government Media Office, which said his death brought the number of journalists killed by Israeli forces in Gaza to 263. Al-Najjar, a father of three, was returned to his family without his head, according to reports from Gaza. Israeli settlers attack Palestinians, steal olive harvest across the occupied West Bank: Salfit: Two Palestinians were by live fire during a settler attack on homes in Yasuf, east of Salfit, on Thursday, according to WAFA. A 50-year-old man was shot in the abdomen and another person was wounded by a bullet fragment in the waist. Israeli forces, who were present during the attack, detained several Palestinians and obstructed an ambulance by taking its key and throwing it away. Jenin: Israeli settlers olives from Palestinian-owned land in Kafr Ra'i, Faqqu'a, Deir Abu Da'if, Ya'bad and other areas near Israeli settlements, as the annual picking season gets underway, WAFA reported. Nablus: Settlers Palestinian farmers picking olives in Odala, south of Nablus, and prevented them from harvesting in the village's plains. Ramallah and Al-Bireh: Settlers olives from Palestinian land in Al-Mughayyir under the protection of Israeli forces. Confrontations broke out as residents attempted to confront the settlers. In Umm Safa, settler bulldozers razed Palestinian land in Wadi Al-Zaytoun and near the village cemetery. Lebanon Israeli attacks continue across south Lebanon despite U.S.-brokered agreement: Nabatieh: Israeli warplanes the outskirts of Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah on Thursday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Overnight, Israeli warplanes also struck the outskirts of Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah, while Israeli artillery intermittently shelled the Ali Al-Taher heights. Tyre (Sour): Israeli forces several homes in Al-Mansouri on Thursday. Israeli warplanes also struck Al-Mansouri. Bint Jbeil: Israeli forces toward Haddatha on Thursday as Israeli military vehicles moved through the town. Lebanon documents suspected Israeli war crimes: Israeli attacks on Lebanon since March 2, 2026, included suspected war crimes and crimes against humanity involving attacks on civilians, journalists, medical personnel, and infrastructure, as well as widespread destruction and forced displacement, according to a more than 200-page compiled by Lebanon's National Committee for International Humanitarian Law and submitted to Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri. The report, according to the New Arab, documents, among other cases, the April 22 killing of journalist Amal Khalil, the April 8 bombardment that killed more than 303 people and wounded over 1,200, and widespread destruction in southern Lebanon, including Bint Jbeil. The report comes despite Lebanon agreeing under the June 26 framework ceasefire to end "all hostile or harmful actions in international political or legal forums" against Israel. Syria and Hezbollah hold first known face-to-face talks in Turkey: Syrian government officials and representatives of Hezbollah in Turkey last month in an effort to ease tensions, marking the first known face-to-face talks between the longtime foes, Reuters reported. The talks, convened at Turkey's initiative, involved Syrian intelligence and foreign ministry officials and Hezbollah representatives. A Syrian official told Reuters that Damascus assured Hezbollah it would not intervene militarily in Lebanon to disarm the group, while asking Hezbollah to help halt cross-border arms smuggling and dismantle alleged remaining cells in Syria. Hezbollah representatives reportedly pledged not to interfere in Syrian affairs but did not directly respond to the other requests. Iran did not participate, although a Lebanese security source said Hezbollah attended with Tehran's knowledge and that Iran was disappointed at being excluded from the talks. U.S. News U.S. economy grew 2.2% in Q2, upgraded from earlier estimate : The U.S. economy at a 2.2 percent annual pace from April through June, the Commerce Department reported Wednesday in its final second-quarter estimate, up from a previous 1.5 percent estimate, surprising economists who had expected little revision. Growth decelerated from 2.5 percent in the first quarter. Consumer spending, which makes up about 70 percent of economic activity, jumped to a 3.8 percent annual pace from just 0.7 percent in the first quarter, while business investment excluding housing rose 9 percent. Tennessee botches second execution this year, governor halts all remaining 2026 executions: The governor of Tennessee has halted the state's remaining executions for the rest of the year after officials were unable to put Christa Gail Pike to death on Wednesday. Pike breathing, talking, and snoring for nearly an hour after receiving two rounds of lethal injection drugs, prompting Tennessee to halt the execution and administer emergency medical care to her. Her attorneys said she was taken to a nearby hospital with no update on her condition Robin Maher , the director of the Death Penalty Information Center, called Wednesday night's execution "one of the worst botched executions in the modern death penalty era." Pike's attorneys had argued that her small veins and a blood disorder created heightened risk of a botched procedure. The incident follows a similarly botched May execution attempt of Tony Carruthers at the same Nashville prison. Republican Gov. Bill Lee halted all remaining 2026 executions after Pike's failed injection and ordered a third-party review of the incident. Hegseth announces new drone command, 20 percent cut to generals in "State of the Force" speech: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at Quantico Wednesday that he is creating a new four-star drone command to oversee autonomous warfare systems, doubling a previous 10 percent reduction in flag and general officer positions to a 20 percent cut, and launching a future-warfare study led by Elon Musk, Newt Gingrich and Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey. The new Autonomous Warfare Command, or AutoWarCom, whose inception Hegseth attributed to the "lessons" learned in Ukraine, will be created despite the recent shuttering of a similar command in Europe. Hegseth also announced plans for a new Office of Religious Affairs and to build a new military base, inviting all 50 states to compete to host the facility, which he estimated could accommodate up to 25,000 service members. FTC launches investigation into OpenAI, Anthropic over AI safety : The Federal Trade Commission is OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies over potential safety risks, Axios reported on Wednesday, with FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson preparing civil investigative demands to compel executives to turn over documents and testify. The probe has reportedly been underway for weeks, and predates OpenAI's disclosure that a model it was testing escaped its sandbox and compromised infrastructure belonging to a startup company, Hugging Face. ICE briefly published, then removed, internal reports showing medical failures in 33 detainee deaths: Internal ICE mortality reviews briefly posted online over the weekend and quickly removed found that the care administered by the agency deviated from "safe practice limit" in 27 of 33 detainee deaths between September 2019 and January 2026, including 11 that occurred since January 2025. In one case, 39-year-old Ismael Ayala-Uribe died from septic shock after Adelanto Processing Center staff failed to examine his abscess, respond to his complaints, or adequately document his care. In another case, 44-year-old Marie Ange Blaise died of a heart attack after staff failed to perform CPR despite finding no pulse. The full report from the San Francisco Chronicle, which first reported on these reviews, is available . DOJ files ethics complaint against nearly all Minnesota federal judges over immigration-surge comments : Attorney General Todd Blanche an ethics complaint Wednesday against nearly all federal district judges in Minnesota, alleging that former Chief Judge Patrick Schiltz, Judge John Tunheim and others violated judicial conduct rules by speaking to the New York Times about the toll of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown. Senate confirms Keith Sonderling as Labor Secretary: The Senate Keith Sonderling , 47-41, as Labor Secretary Wednesday, elevating Sonderling, who had served as acting secretary since April, to the top job. Sonderling, a Trump first-term advisor and former Republican EEOC member, succeeds Lori Chavez-DeRemer , who left the post following accusations that she abused her position. Sen. Josh Hawley introduces bill to regulate Flock cameras, AI surveillance : Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) is the Stop Flock Abuse Act to impose stricter data, security, and search limits on automated license plate readers like Flock cameras. The bill would restrict local governments from selling or sharing vehicle data, require data deletion within 10 days absent an active criminal investigation, ban facial recognition on surveillance networks, and mandate written approval and audit logs to prevent unauthorized searches. Data would also need to be encrypted and kept within the U.S. Commerce Secretary Lutnick reports over $250 million in income from 2025: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick 's newly released 2025 financial disclosure he reported at least $250 million in income and proceeds. The largest part of this was a $192 million "tax distribution" from Cantor Fitzgerald, the financial firm he led for decades before stepping down to join the administration. He also disclosed $4.2 million in salary and bonus from the real estate firm Newmark, $19.6 million from a Newmark partnership exchange, $14.1 million from the brokerage BGC Group, and over $5 million from BGC restricted stock units. Judge rules U.S. can deport Milwaukee Muslim leader on national security grounds : Immigration Judge Jayme Salinardi Wednesday that Salah Sarsour, president of the Islamic Society of Milwaukee and a prominent Palestinian rights advocate, can be deported on foreign policy grounds, though she rejected the government's separate claim that he lied on his green card application. The ruling follows Sarsour's detention in March and a ruling by a federal judge in June ordering his release, which noted that he had made a "substantial" claim that the government had targeted him for his pro-Palestinian activism. Sarsour, who called the ruling "deeply disappointing," said he will appeal and that deportation to the occupied West Bank, where he was born and previously imprisoned by Israel, would "mean the end of my life." Sarsour's attorneys say he was tortured and coerced into confessions during his 1988 and 1995 convictions in Israel. Sarsour has lived in the U.S. since 1993. During his detention by ICE, Sarsour, who has Type 2 diabetes, lost more than 30 pounds. According to his attorneys, his blood sugar levels were checked only once a month, putting him at risk of organ failure or death. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Bolivian attorney general detained days after U.S. revoked his visa over alleged drug trafficking ties: Police detained Attorney General Roger Mariaca on Wednesday and the prosecutor's offices in Sucre. Washington imposed visa restrictions on Mariaca and accused him on Monday of accepting bribes to facilitate drug trafficking and help violent criminals evade justice. Mariaca denied the allegations, calling the visa restrictions "interference" and "political pressure" in response to his investigations. Mariaca has been involved in of Trump-linked figures accused of corruption and violent crimes including Argentinian political consultant Fernando Cerimedo who is facing drug-trafficking charges in addition to the charge of attempted murder after allegedly ordering a hit on his former girlfriend Nadia Beller. In response to the visa restrictions imposed on Bolivian officials, Beller published a photo showing Cerimedo in a meeting with Donald Trump Junior and MAGA political operator Brad Parscale. She alleged the raid on Mariana's office was an effort to "disappear" evidence in the Cerimedo case. For more on Cerimedo and President Rodrigo Paz 's effort to distance himself from his onetime key adviser, read Joseph Bouchard's report for Drop Site . Pakistan says strikes killed 22 fighters in Afghanistan; Kabul claims civilian deaths : Pakistan's Ministry of Information airstrikes based on "credible intelligence" killed at least 22 fighters from the Pakistani Taliban (TTP) and Balochistan Liberation Army at camps and hideouts in Afghanistan, destroying weapons and ammunition caches. A spokesman for the Afghan Taliban said the attacks hit Afghanistan's Kunar and Helmand provinces late Wednesday, and that they killed at least nine people, including women and children, wounded 11 others and destroyed three houses. Afghanistan denies harboring armed groups and says recent Pakistani strikes have repeatedly hit civilian homes. Russia warns NATO it would use nuclear weapons if alliance blocks Kaliningrad : Russia a diplomatic memo to NATO member states Wednesday warning it is prepared to use its "entire arsenal, including nuclear weapons," if the alliance attempts to blockade the Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad, claiming it has "information that NATO is preparing an air and naval blockade" of the territory. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte called the document "unhelpful" and said Russia should "stop the nuclear threats," adding that NATO is a defensive alliance and claiming that "Putin knows that he can never win" in a confrontation with the group. Brazil briefs French, German officials on alleged U.S. and Russian election interference : Brazil's spy agency Abin a visiting French and German delegation in Brasilia this month, "confirming the existence of interference from the United States as well as Russia" ahead of Brazil's Sunday election, according to Reuters. The agency alleged that U.S. interference ranged "from lawfare to interference that is openly acknowledged"; no details were given related to the alleged Russian activity. A senior Brazilian cyber official present at the briefing also noted that cyberattacks targeting Brazil's president's office have nearly doubled and are "clearly election-related." In , philosopher Rodrigo Nunes, political scientist Camila Rocha, journalist Piero Locatelli and organizer Stephanie Weatherbee Brito examine the stakes of the election. Their essays assess the resilience of Bolsonarismo, the growing role of U.S. intervention, the weakening of Brazil's left, and the challenges facing popular movements. Gunmen kill 7 on Syrian bus; gas pipeline blast knocks out three power plants : Unidentified gunmen on a civilian bus carrying workers home in Homs, Syria, Wednesday, killing at least seven people, Syrian state media reported. The shooting came hours after an explosion and fire at a gas pipeline in eastern Ghouta near Damascus knocked the Deir Ali, al-Nasiriyah, and Tishreen power plants offline, with Energy Minister Mohammed al-Bashir saying the cause of the explosion remains unclear. "It could be a technical malfunction, an attack or an act of sabotage," he said. Wednesday's explosion was the third such pipeline incident in six weeks, following two earlier blasts the Syrian Petroleum Company attributed to sabotage, with no group claiming responsibility for any of the attacks. U.S. removes Syria from arms export ban: The U.S. State Department Syria from its ITAR ("International Traffic in Arms Regulations") arms export denial list in a notice published Wednesday, effective Thursday. Syrian requests to purchase arms from U.S. companies will now be considered on a case-by-case basis. Only seven countries--Belarus, China, Cuba, Iran, Myanmar, North Korea, and Venezuela--remain subject to the policy. The move follows President Trump's easing of decades-old sanctions on Syria last year and Secretary of State Marco Rubio's August rescission of Syria's state sponsor of terrorism designation, part of a broader warming toward President Ahmad al-Sharaa's government. Iraqi armed group suspends military operations after U.S. troop withdrawal : Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed Iraqi militia and political movement, Wednesday that it was ceasing military activities following the departure of U.S. forces. The withdrawal concludes the U.S.-led military mission in Iraq that began in 2014 to fight the Islamic State. The group had previously said it would only discuss giving up its weapons once foreign troops left. Iraq's government said talks were ongoing to bring armed groups into state institutions, but Kataib Hezbollah's announcement did not include a commitment to disarm. China builds new military facility in Laos, possibly first full PLA base in Southeast Asia: China's defense ministry on Tuesday that the China-Laos Joint Support and Training Center and the China-Laos Friendship Aviation Academy are now operational in Ban Keun, on the outskirts of the Laotian capital of Vientiane. Satellite imagery reviewed by Reuters appears to show that the center features a newly constructed airfield, which includes a paved runway, a taxiway, an apron, and new buildings. China's defense ministry said the facility trains air force pilots and is "not directed against any third party." Security scholar Collin Koh wrote on X that the base "may not be wrong to conclude this is the first full-fledged PLA overseas base in Southeast Asia," distinguishing it from China's more ambiguous joint training center at Cambodia's Ream naval base. The facility adds to China's growing overseas military footprint, which already includes a Djibouti base, artificial island facilities in the Spratly Islands, and reported new construction in the disputed Paracel archipelago. Norway 's parliament probes PM Støre, 10 others over Epstein links: Norway's Parliament a public hearing Wednesday into 11 current and former senior officials, including Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre, over ties to Jeffrey Epstein allegedly revealed in the files released by the U.S. Justice Department in January. The scrutiny centers on the diplomat Terje Rod-Larsen, who ran the International Peace Institute and who had numerous ties to the financier. It has been alleged that Rod-Larsen secured an illicit loan from Epstein and helped the financier commit visa fraud for the women he trafficked; Epstein also reportedly left millions to Rod-Larsen's children in his will. The announcement follows recent reporting that the foreign ministry allocated over 130 million kroner ($13.5 million) to the Institute while Rod-Larsen was in charge and while he reportedly was engaged with Epstein. Støre, who served as foreign minister while Terje Rod-Larsen ran the IPI, has denied he had any relationship with Epstein. Hong Kong journalist arrested on sedition charge over 2019 police clash coverage : Hong Kong police Tang Ho-wing, founder of the outlet Boom News, on Wednesday on suspicion of "incitement by spreading disinformation," after his outlet posted a video featuring a woman's account of a 2019 attack at the Prince Edward rail station, where anti-government protesters say police officers killed some in their cohort. Authorities also arrested another person, identified as activist Lee Ying-chi by the South China Morning Post, alongside Tang on Wednesday. South Africa summons U.S. Ambassador Bozell for third time over "undiplomatic conduct": South Africa's foreign affairs ministry U.S. Ambassador Leo Brent Bozell III on Tuesday for the third time in his nine-month tenure over what officials described as "undiplomatic conduct," a South African official told Reuters. The precise cause of the demarche is not known. The State Department confirmed that Bozell met with his South African counterparts, claiming that they "discussed bilateral ties" and adding that the U.S. is "not interested in diplomatic manoeuvring, procedural delays or dialogue for dialogue's sake." The summons comes amid deteriorating relations fueled by President Donald Trump's repeated unsubstantiated claims that white South Africans face systemic persecution; it also follows the U.S.'s announcement of additional visa restrictions on South Africans two weeks ago. French court sentences 13 to prison over 2021 Channel crossing that killed 31 migrants : A Paris court 13 men on Wednesday for organizing the deadliest small-boat migrant crossing attempt to the UK, with six convicted of involuntary homicide (which carries as many as 10 years in prison) and the remaining seven receiving lesser sentences of up to four years; a 14th defendant was acquitted. Prosecutors alleged that the defendants put a vessel to sea that was unfit for the crossing, overloaded the vessel with migrants (primarily Iraqi Kurds), and failed to provide lifejackets for the voyage. The vessel, which attempted a crossing of the English Channel in November 2021, capsized, killing 31 migrants. Seven French military personnel remain under investigation for allegedly failing to assist survivors during the incident. MI5 warns UK academics to sever ties with Chinese research group over alleged spying : Britain's MI5 a rare public alert Wednesday accusing the China General Technology Research Institute of having "very strong ties" to China's Ministry of State Security, adding that the group's "primary purpose" is funding academic research that enhances Chinese espionage capabilities. The statement warned that more than 100 UK-based academics working in AI, cybersecurity, covert communications and steganography had been targeted by the group, and told academics that, should they continue accepting CGTRI grants, they could be prosecuted under the UK's 2023 National Security Act. Rwanda open to hosting EU migrant transfer facilities, lawmakers say : Rwanda has preliminary discussions with some EU member states about potentially hosting facilities for migrants transferred from Europe, European Parliament lawmakers Tineke Strik and Anna Strolenberg said Wednesday after a visit to Kigali, though no agreements have been reached. An EU official told Reuters that Rwanda is among the countries being considered by the "Group of Five"--Germany, Austria, Greece, Denmark, and the Netherlands--which announced earlier this month they aim to establish migrant "return hubs" outside the EU this year. Rwanda has increasingly positioned itself as a destination for Western deportations, previously receiving up to 250 migrants from the U.S. as part of a 2025 agreement. Entire newsroom arrested in Egypt in significant press crackdown: Six journalists from the independent Egyptian investigative journalism platform Matsda2sh--comprising the media outlet's entire newsroom--were arrested by Egyptian security forces overnight on Monday in an escalated crackdown on press freedoms in Egypt, to Mada Masr. The condition and whereabouts of their detention remains unknown and they remain forcibly disappeared. The Interior Ministry on Thursday the arrests for the first time and accused Matsda2sh of fabricating lies and spreading rumors to "undermine stability," and accused the outlet of having ties to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood. The platform's founder Abdelrahman Mansour, rejected the accusations in a statement, saying the authorities know the charges--which are commonly levelled by Egyptian authorities against journalists--are false. "I believe this is the first time in the two-century history of Egyptian journalism that an entire newsroom, with all its journalists, has been arrested," Hossam Bahgat, of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, told Mada Masr. Over 50 civil society organizations and independent media outlets around the world have signed a calling for the immediate release of the six journalists. Before the latest arrests, Egypt ranked as the 7th worst jailer of journalists in the world, according to the latest CPJ census. Peter, Tonight is a big night for this campaign – and for Maine.

**At 7:00 PM tonight, Rick takes the debate stage** in Portland for the first gubernatorial debate of the general election, hosted by News Center Maine in partnership with the Maine State Chamber of Commerce. He'll answer questions side by side with Hannah Pingree and Bobby Charles and **make the case that Maine needs an independent Governor who puts Mainers first, not parties or politics.**

**Here's how to watch live, wherever you are in Maine:**
* On TV: News Center Maine WCSH Channel 6 (Portland/southern Maine) or WLBZ Channel 2 (Bangor/eastern Maine), over the air or on cable
* On your phone or tablet: Stream free on the News Center Maine app
* On your smart TV: Download the News Center Maine app on Roku, Apple TV, or Fire TV and watch live
* Online: Stream live at [newscentermaine.com/watch](newscentermaine.com/watch)

---

Make homeownership possible again for working families. Deliver real property tax relief. And fix a state government that has become slow, opaque, and unaccountable to the people it serves.

**Here's how you can help tonight:** watch with family and neighbors, forward this email to three friends who need to hear Rick's message, and follow along with us on social media during the debate.

**Mainers deserve a governor who will make government work for them.** Tonight, Rick gets to make that case to all of Maine with you behind him.

**Thank you for everything you do,** Bennett for Governor Team

| Peter —

From all of us at the Center for Reproductive Rights, I want to say **thank you.**

Because of your generosity we not only met but _exceeded_ our flash match goal. Every single dollar is doubled to protect, defend, and expand access to reproductive care.

The support of people like you is why we can represent patients like Magon Hoffman in Oklahoma after she was denied emergency abortion care following her baby’s fatal fetal diagnosis.

**Donations to the Center provide the critical resources we need to challenge abortion bans in 10 states and push back against the abuses of the Trump administration with 30+ active filings.**

We fight legal battles, but they also represent real women, real families, and real lives that extreme anti-abortion restrictions have upended.

[There's still time to make a gift and support these women and millions more who need a fighter in their corner.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/140425219/650453535/2141984067?sourceid=1151619&utm_campaign=27emage-0915aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=thanks&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0YWRjMjJjZS1hOGJkLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=t_-UmBCQSHP5dNy26ZGvlvOsKo_0JTI3k2Z4iBZdAc0=&emci=b5dbf71b-65b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=4adc22ce-a8bd-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=954237) We are so grateful to have you with us — and ready for whatever comes next.

Onward,

Nancy Northup

name: Kailee for Congress
subject: Official invitation for Peter
body:
I want you beside me as we build this campaign from the ground up.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/f8OfxvTg8CC?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Peter, I wanted to personally thank you for joining our campaign.
I grew up in Auburn in a blue-collar family. My dad spent 41 years working as a correctional officer. My mom is a nurse who cares for Alzheimer’s patients. I worked multiple jobs to put myself through school, became the first person in my family to earn a four-year degree, and spent years paying off my student loans.
_I know what it means to work hard, do everything right, and still wonder why it keeps getting harder to get ahead._
**That is why I’m running for Congress: to lower costs, protect our communities, defend our farmers and small businesses, and make Central New York a place where our children can build their futures.**
But this campaign doesn't just belong to me. It belongs to every New Yorker who is ready to fight for something better.
_That means you, too._
Because you joined us at the very beginning, I’m inviting you to become an official FOUNDING MEMBER of Kailee Buller for Congress.
---
| [ACCEPT YOUR FOUNDING MEMBERSHIP >> ](https://us.list-manage.com/1NNS_SjwyxV?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
---
| |
I want you to understand the responsibility that comes along with being a Founding Member.
These will be the people we rely on the most to share opinions and keep us in touch with every little thing that goes on in Central New York. We'll need to know who needs our help and who could use a yard sign, or a sticker, or anything like that.
We'll also be keeping you in the loop with all of the exclusive campaign-only memos and polls to keep you up-to-date on any important news the campaign receives.
_You'll be our best tool for sharing important updates with your friends and family._
Can I count on you to do that, Peter?
I hope so.
[**And I hope you accept the invitation to become an OFFICIAL Founding Member of the campaign.**](https://us.list-manage.com/TOHTAROxc8s?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
Once you do, keep an eye on your inbox for any exclusive news.
And Peter, heads up...
**This offer won’t last long. Our Founding Member invite is only going to our staunchest supporters, so make sure you sign up as soon as possible.**

I’m honored to have you on this team. Let’s get to work.
Kailee BullerRepublican Candidate for Congress, NY-22

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** Thursday, October 1, 2026 Contact: Maddy Rosen maddy@caitconley.com **
**
### CAIT CONLEY RAISES OVER $5 MILLION IN Q3 OF 2026
******************OSSINING, NY –** Army combat veteran and Democratic nominee for New York’s 17th Congressional District Cait Conley raised **over $5 million in the third quarter of 2026, bringing the total cycle raise to $9.5 million**. The campaign received **more than 44,000 contributions** , with an **average contribution of $118**. Unlike her opponent, Rep. Mike Lawler, who has raked in over $1 million in corporate PAC donations, **Cait Conley has never taken any corporate PAC money** and instead is fueled by thousands of grassroots supporters in New York and across the country. The massive fundraising haul comes as a new [Emerson College Polling / PIX11 News poll](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.HV-T5b9C6Y6Pisqo-P4Pm-8Vmis2a7yX6D4Js9PPBQZSK7U-2Zj-qKGJGAdFsPGsghCObOql_AgtCej_v6LInY1yDv_dUWTIOeiZlcevIPG99Xw39G7ty6plplabD90cX6GllaEA6oFEakWxDa03XmUKg9AkRCLzZyjY1TFFIZ3bfGi-Uqp2TnXHywdfe8G8LSq0tX2M6HaPFtgVj3foS1JwW7dNzh72YNKkmL8cra4-wfLVgmRR0oM-a2rt68SFqPUUMQxb1xeDqXYeXCrzwoolTSo8VDmqidoEMI5o0CutUuhXE4AjXXuFdOVd083tBem4PEiaCaFwnpGYpR25v1vuSCUi-eoBmDAexd34lDk/4ui/wHDzipsfQRm29SHYuKUL9Q/h0/h001.LUDj3XlkwBu0uiXaWYrGk3joF9C8E3fO_CU1YVByfXU) released this morning finds **Cait Conley up 48% to 46% against Mike Lawler** in the race to represent NY-17. **Cait Conley spokesperson Maddy Rosen:** _“Momentum and excitement are building behind Army combat veteran Cait Conley, as voters across NY-17 prepare to send career political operative and former utility lobbyist Mike Lawler packing on November 3rd. While Mike votes with Donald Trump 100% of the time — even when it makes his constituents’ lives harder and more expensive — Cait will take on anyone who stands in the way of the better, more affordable future the Hudson Valley deserves.”_ __ ### **About Cait Conley** Cait Conley is a Hudson Valley native, the daughter of a postal worker and a construction worker. She applied to West Point the day after 9/11 and went on to serve in the Army, first as a military police officer and then in special operations leadership, deploying six times and earning three Bronze Stars. Cait concluded her active-duty career as Director for Counterterrorism at the National Security Council, where Russia sanctioned her for her work, and then served as a senior executive at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, protecting critical infrastructure and the systems that run our elections. She put her life on the line to serve this country, not any person or political party, and especially not corporate special interests. Now, Cait is running to take on corruption so politicians can’t keep lining their pockets at the taxpayers’ expense, including by banning stock trading; lowering middle-class taxes; and holding monopoly utility companies and Big Pharma accountable to lower costs. To learn more, visit [caitconley.com](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.BMyXzJRPwu_AnDhWGQjUxHaFuvXbS1BlNO-Lh096nHqkTD1yAB5wHbqy9W-YoCildw2aZZZgbNmDjV67KXtx9rHKk4KMlYM7Qm0CgCtPVvEwjldqXRgRmIL7IMqW2kJAgx6mn7HxnBy-03OhgUrFu75EJW5xlKvUBmxgH2tYQhz35wtOGlFWjHVFsxr4gPt2ZFdAgYPlXEZs7v4D4_VMv3gKKmHJr7EL8OKqjfVT7zPkRHFdeounDNsxSinFgYM4aY9AVmQ9JmyMKRyoVAHPxFYn7I72QhR99km2sJ672aLc57R1aAiGFK4r5Gcq8GXw/4ui/wHDzipsfQRm29SHYuKUL9Q/h1/h001.C3UTV_OMzWxsa2e9Jnl1JVOhMoSSF34p-0MLaSpvilM).

The massive fundraising haul comes as a new released this morning finds Cait Conley up 48% to 46% against Mike Lawler in the race to represent NY-17. Cait Conley spokesperson Maddy Rosen: “Momentum and excitement are building behind Army combat veteran Cait Conley, as voters across NY-17 prepare to send career political operative and former utility lobbyist Mike Lawler packing on November 3rd. While Mike votes with Donald Trump 100% of the time — even when it makes his constituents’ lives harder and more expensive — Cait will take on anyone who stands in the way of the better, more affordable future the Hudson Valley deserves.” ### About Cait Conley Cait Conley is a Hudson Valley native, the daughter of a postal worker and a construction worker. She applied to West Point the day after 9/11 and went on to serve in the Army, first as a military police officer and then in special operations leadership, deploying six times and earning three Bronze Stars. Cait concluded her active-duty career as Director for Counterterrorism at the National Security Council, where Russia sanctioned her for her work, and then served as a senior executive at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, protecting critical infrastructure and the systems that run our elections. She put her life on the line to serve this country, not any person or political party, and especially not corporate special interests. Now, Cait is running to take on corruption so politicians can’t keep lining their pockets at the taxpayers’ expense, including by banning stock trading; lowering middle-class taxes; and holding monopoly utility companies and Big Pharma accountable to lower costs. Meet Joe Males:

**Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission.

Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved.

Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he’s determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same.

Joe’s entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy.

During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met.

Team, First, I want to say thank you. **Because of this grassroots team, Fight Like Hell PAC hit our end-of-quarter goal last night.** I’m incredibly grateful to everyone who chipped in, shared our message, or showed up for this work. And a few days ago, I had the chance to speak at the Human Rights Campaign’s annual dinner. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140430632/650469209/-1313101072?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&refcode=AU_FLHP_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20261001_PM1_V1_S2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDY0NjIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOGUyYzkyNDYtYWRiZC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=P5dhDHpVupFfqcQ9VYHx1O0tDiDnlYnwMThi2-XEkZE=) I told the room something I want you to hear, too: **You deserve to love who you love. You deserve to be who you are. And you deserve to be treated with dignity and respect — no matter what.** Those aren’t abstract ideas to me. Fundamental freedoms are about having the power to make decisions about your own life: when and how to start a family, whether you can see a doctor without going broke, whether you can get a job, find a home, start a business, and live safely as the person you are. In Michigan, we’ve worked to turn those values into law. We expanded civil rights protections for LGBTQ+ Michiganders, banned the so-called panic defense, created our state’s first LGBTQ+ commission, and supported LGBTQ+ entrepreneurs and businesses. One of the proudest moments of my life came when I signed the expansion to the _Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act_ with my daughter Sherry standing beside me, protecting every Michigander, no matter who they love or how they identify. Sherry came out to me while she was applying to college. I didn’t know I was raising a gay daughter all those years — _but I’m damn proud I did._ **As a parent, there is nothing I won’t do to protect my kids. And as governor, there is nothing I won’t do to protect yours.** That’s the message I wanted to leave with everyone at HRC: that progress can feel slow, and the attacks can be relentless, but _movements are built by people who keep showing up anyway._ We’ve seen what that looks like before. Marriage equality. The repeal of “Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell.” Stronger protections against hate crimes. More than a thousand out and proud LGBTQ+ elected officials serving across the country. None of that happened because people gave up when the fight got hard. And with the midterms just weeks away, there is still a lot of work in front of us. **[If you didn't get a chance to pitch in before our end-of-quarter goal, we could use you today. If you can think of an example of everyday people holding huge corporations accountable for harming the public, it was probably made possible in large part by a [single legal theory](https://substack.com/redirect/72ed6b10-83d8-4ffa-8e98-3e2a6ff71487?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): public nuisance.
Public nuisance was a primary basis for the litigation against Big Tobacco in the 1990s, and was the foundation of the opioid cases over the past decade. It's played a prominent role in lawsuits on lead paint, predatory lending, water pollution, and "forever chemicals" like PFAS. It was the most important hook in recent [successful cases](https://substack.com/redirect/1b3b777e-82b9-41db-86cc-62911694dfe3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against social media companies like Meta for designing their platforms to addict and endanger children. And most recently, it has been a key cause of action in [litigation](https://substack.com/redirect/429a0dec-0720-4c6e-ad58-63b66dfa3b16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in several states against data centers for the air, water, and noise pollution they cause.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=218333183&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE4MzMzMTgzLCJpYXQiOjE3OTA4Njk2MjYsImV4cCI6MTc5MzQ2MTYyNiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.GJGyp72bI-TU3mv1oe4I_KsRZ-vKYoTahj9RL_yuUBU)
But not in Utah, Kansas, or Montana. Though it largely passed under the national radar, these states [enacted](https://substack.com/redirect/0742086f-d5f4-49c2-9869-1f3e923a8c79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [laws](https://substack.com/redirect/14b3624e-0a21-43e8-aa22-d46fe18fb283?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this year or [last](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02ee84-6f93-4d7f-8b64-45e6706fecc7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that dismantle public nuisance as a cause of action--laws that, according to the Utah State Legislature's own Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel, will make claims against data centers and other corporate wrongdoers "more difficult to pursue." These states are not outliers, either--they're forerunners. Their laws closely mirror a model bill published this summer by the American Legislative Exchange Council, the corporate oligarchy's [primary conduit](https://substack.com/redirect/fb6975e4-b5bf-4955-852a-0c5f839cb3e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for [enacting right-wing laws](https://substack.com/redirect/784c6a16-7fb1-435e-a3c9-97df3a074e25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the state level. As I write this, ALEC's [Public Nuisance Reform Act](https://substack.com/redirect/90d47c35-c6f3-41bd-98cd-21924fee6ecf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is likely being distributed to Republican legislators in dozens of state houses around the country--and you can bet that Big Tech, eager to suppress a valuable tool of data center opponents, is lining up lobbyists to coax its passage.
Indeed, if this year was about trialing this extremist proposal, leaders on the ground believe that next year the real onslaught will begin. "Big corporations and the politicians they purchase use states like Utah as a testing ground for their regressive agenda," Utah state Senator Nate Blouin, a Democrat, told me. "But make no mistake, these corporate immunity laws are coming for you wherever you are. I wouldn't be surprised if they get introduced in nearly every state next year."
These attacks on public nuisance law constitute just one offensive in a multi-front war the right has been waging against our ability to use the courts to hold the wealthy and powerful to account. On October 5, the Supreme Court will hear _Suncor v. Boulder_ , in which Big Oil companies will make their case for immunity from legal repercussions for the fires, droughts, air pollution, extreme heat, and other harms they've caused to communities.
Boulder, the Colorado county and city, sued Suncor and Exxon Mobil in 2018 over the damage that climate change--and the companies' lies about their role in fueling it--had done to its residents. After the state Supreme Court ruled that the case should go to trial, Suncor and Exxon Mobil--clearly terrified of what would happen if communities like Boulder were allowed to have their day in court--asked the high court to intervene, arguing in legal briefs that "state tort law is not the solution to global climate change." As TNR's Matt Ford [wrote recently](https://substack.com/redirect/0be712cd-b059-4c0a-8b0a-362ffe0a3e5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the companies "effectively argue that because they and their products have caused damage everywhere, they cannot be held liable for it anywhere."
In case the Supreme Court doesn't give Big Oil a get-out-of-jail-free card, it's pursuing other means. In addition to its public nuisance model bill, ALEC recently published the [Energy Producers and Consumers Protection Act](https://substack.com/redirect/b0503f7d-bb99-4f1a-9617-6515364251ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which immunizes all corporations--the fossil fuel industry, certainly, but also all other industries--from liability for any misconduct that is even marginally related to climate change, including "negligence, gross negligence, recklessness, strict liability, products liability, failure to warn, fraud, fraudulent concealment, misrepresentation, unjust enrichment," as well as all related "criminal charges, indictments, or prosecutions." In other words, under this legislation, fraud is legal--if you're a powerful corporation. Meanwhile, Texas Senator Ted Cruz has introduced similar [legislation](https://substack.com/redirect/84b93c17-8baf-4deb-9334-59c4db68c514?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the federal level.
This right-wing blitzkrieg to shield big business from liability for its misconduct extends far beyond the issue of climate change. On a recent Federalist Society panel about climate immunity for corporations, O.H. Skinner, the executive director of Alliance for Consumers--one of numerous front groups spun up by conservative legal activist Leonard Leo--[explained](https://substack.com/redirect/0af334ef-d181-4338-800e-dd66b5a045e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that these efforts need to cover not just fossil fuel companies but every major industry, from Big Ag to Big Tech: "A lot of people in this space only talk about climate. And it frustrates me ... I'm the kind of person that, because I care about all these products, I start thinking, well [Big Oil immunity] doesn't do anything about pork, and it doesn't do anything about AI regulation." Earlier this year, the Supreme Court also issued a [ruling](https://substack.com/redirect/70707697-98ec-41a5-ac45-a42ac1ff5745?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) protecting Monsanto and other pesticide producers from thousands of lawsuits by families and farmworkers devastated by the cancer-causing effects of glyphosate products like Roundup.
This effort really does represent an attempt to fundamentally restructure our corporate governance model in the U.S., which has always relied on robust private litigation. All the way back in 1803, Chief Justice John Marshall, in his famous _Marbury v. Madison_ decision, wrote that the "very essence of civil liberty certainly consists in the right of every individual to claim the protection of the laws, whenever he receives an injury." While most developed countries overwhelmingly rely on public enforcement of laws, private enforcement--not just to compensate injured parties, but to affirmatively deter corporate malfeasance--has [long played](https://substack.com/redirect/fb81ab5c-7544-4528-aceb-514fd2f54d47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a key role in America, where regulatory state capacity has traditionally been much weaker than in places like Europe. This dynamic has become even more pronounced in recent years, as far-right billionaires have succeeded in dismantling significant portions of the administrative state and stacking federal regulatory offices with shills for the industries they're supposed to be regulating. In this context, public nuisance litigation and other lawsuits that rely on state law are communities' last--and sometimes only--line of defense against the unchecked avarice of powerful corporations that have been fully unleashed by the Trump administration.
So it's no wonder that the oligarchy has set its sights on dismantling the basic architecture of our civil legal system. This isn't an entirely new effort: The corporate right has been waging a version of this war, whitewashed as "tort reform," for decades. But to outright immunize corporate wrongdoing across the board--from Big Oil's climate crimes to Big Tech's data center disasters--would be a whole new level of elite impunity. The oligarchs are coming for every last tool the American people have ever used to restrain corporate abuse, deception, and overreach. And the fight to save these rights will be happening right in your community, no matter where in America you live.

subject: We’re adding 5 new “Reach” races to our map!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
How we leverage a strong November for Democrats.
#
Hi there,
You’ve surely heard that the midterms are looking good for Democrats. With Dems consistently polling higher than Republicans on the generic congressional ballot and Trump’s approval rating at an all-time low, the national environment is creating new opportunities to win seats across the country.
**Given these strong signals, today we’re releasing a brand-new way for you to support candidates in the toughest-to-win districts: the[Reach Fund](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-reach-races-2026.tCUTQu&refcode=em20261001-2992&t=1&akid=2992%2E1562180%2EtEYwvQ), which is dedicated entirely to our “Reach” races!**
So far this cycle, Swing Left has focused on directing grassroots donations to the Must-Win races on our map. But with the possibility of a big swing toward Democrats this November, we’ve heard from many of you that you want the opportunity to support an even broader slate of candidates.
Flipping the House, flipping the Senate, and winning critical state-level seats is not guaranteed. We still need to do everything we can to secure the path to winning Democratic majorities, and our Immediate Impact Fund—updated regularly—will continue to be the best investment you can make at any time through Election Day.
**For grassroots donors also interested in taking a bigger swing, we’re debuting the Reach Fund.** The Reach Races are more of a stretch based on past results, current polling, or the partisan makeup of the district or state. But they are also a key part of our long-term strategy—because these are places where the political environment is shifting, where we can reach new voters, and where deeper organizing can strengthen the Democratic brand.
Investing in these places now could win us an extra seat; if not, it builds groundwork that will make it easier for a Democrat to win next time. We know going in that we likely won’t win all of our Reach Races. But with control of the Senate now within reach this November, and with limited chances to win more seats in 2028 and 2030, we have to treat each seat as an opportunity to compete.

So if you’re the kind of person who likes to take chances and wants to invest in tougher races, this fund is for you.
**The candidates the Reach Fund will support include all 13 races on the current Swing Left “Reach” swing districts and state targets list, plus 5 brand-new candidates that our political team is adding to our map today. These include:**
* **Florida’s 7th Congressional District, Democrat Bale Dalton:** Former NASA chief of staff Bale Dalton was running against scandal-plagued Republican Rep. Cory Mills, who lost the GOP primary in August. Now, Dalton heads into the general election with a cash advantage over his Republican opponent. While Trump won this district by 12% in 2024, his margin was half that in 2020, giving Dalton a real shot in this political climate, especially if he can continue raising resources.

* **Florida’s 27th Congressional District, Democrat Eliott Rodriguez:** Republican Rep. Maria Salazar’s recent high-profile ad distancing herself from Trump on immigration shows that she knows she is vulnerable in this heavily Latino district that Democrats flipped in the 2018 blue wave. Rodriguez, a former TV anchor, is putting up a strong fight to tie Salazar to Trump’s unpopular and harmful policies.

* **Nevada’s 2nd Congressional District, Democrat Teresa Benitez-Thompson:** Recent polling shows this race more competitive than expected, as former Assembly Majority Leader Benitez-Thompson is running a strong campaign against a wealthy and extreme MAGA opponent who the outgoing Republican incumbent has refused to endorse.

* **Florida Governor, Democrat David Jolly:** While Florida has drifted to the right since the rise of Trump, a recent poll showed Democratic nominee Jolly, a former Republican member of Congress, leading his GOP opponent, U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds, by 3 points. In this political climate, Jolly is looking to build a winning coalition of voters impacted by rising costs in Florida, a home insurance crisis, and data centers, but only if he can compete with Donalds’ massive campaign bank account.

* **New Hampshire Governor, Democrat Cinde Warmington:** New Hampshire is one of the two states in the country that have a Republican governor but were won by Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024. While New Hampshire has been blue on the federal level since 2004, Republicans have held the governor’s mansion since 2017. Cinde Warmington, a former elected member of the state’s unique Executive Council, is running a strong campaign against incumbent Governor Kelly Ayotte. 62% of NH voters disapprove of Trump and Warmington is looking to leverage this to an upset win.

[**If you’d like to support candidates in “Reach” races like the ones above, click here to make a donation to our new Reach Fund today.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-reach-races-2026.tCUTQu&refcode=em20261001-2992&t=2&akid=2992%2E1562180%2EtEYwvQ)
**[Donate Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-reach-races-2026.tCUTQu&refcode=em20261001-2992&t=3&akid=2992%2E1562180%2EtEYwvQ)**
Together, we’re going to power Democrats all over the country to victory this November and beyond. So thank you, as always, for everything you do.
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20261001-1&t=4&refcode2=2992_1562180_tEYwvQ&akid=2992%2E1562180%2EtEYwvQ)

Peter,

You've never received an email from me before. Maybe you've never heard my name. Allow me to explain.

I'm Nick Searcy. I produced the films _Capitol Punishment_ and _The War on Truth_ to show people what really happened on January 6. I'm also a proud supporter of Stand in the Gap Foundation, a nonprofit on a mission to provide the help, hope, and healing J6ers need to succeed in their second chance.

Today, especially in the next sixty minutes, I want to reach as many people as I can with this request.

I set a goal to raise $20,000 before the end of the month for Stand in the Gap so they can help former J6ers and their families rebuild their lives, with legal aid, health care coverage, counseling, housing support, and most importantly, hope.

[If that is all you need to hear, please contribute $10 or whatever you can afford by clicking here.](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=c7b82e7143ac4dc894d403c92acdfd14&_e=db6bZeZW7KYkDA68vcaLauCxCErU85beDmh4kH_c9avwYf3Icwj1iMphXApg8p1IKzQFAfrld4zHCZSkREWl8qF5YnquWf3r288Lg_MHC5u8UFfoM1ignDx3sJetZAe8WsQG_kenw-1rpl4H3YcbULASp-II1o6x9iSCBfQv7a494ALSDAKRc8PlThmkaCSstIho_OAvDNIU0KAgDY42nDCJgzeCezt4BCRouz2cS8rvSD2u083k9W9xhyeQEjn46EZPKJxj_44wF7FbI3rnXrYKAfhk2Z2PwBDUg5z7b-XtBcU0NTIrfOJwC5U3rfRhn1aOya4W7OEKo65C3nO0F11Vssu7cbR9lQpHiWBkTwv8bn4YBhY6_TI_kmhe24KbaJgiZcB2sqiAW2wI5unAiFR8tDqV5FFKUcPBl9xdZflZcUoBlZz1J7w44W9yJjf4mhcu_cJDXpMFm_18-F8zkk8ShTSqnsR7FG-GAaHHKxBbL-9qRxMm8OQ-mzrWWliD_0LoCKRqUOZYzi1Rj9fTuB_DqrGsKfMYNyfl1dFmPcHJlbbYWhA7-59dmkR4xQLZ6mdTE3CT1vxcoXOZSASsFqVWSk1rlMiymXucnaDImGoKLdgR7zpKqAW7m1NjdDuikiwexolHMRZm8kY879cpvw%3D%3D)

Otherwise, let me explain why I'm asking you to donate today:

$10 because Governor Gavin Newsom is still persecuting J6ers by recently signing legislation that imposes a 100% California tax on distributions from President Trump's compensation fund established for victims of the January 6 prosecutions.

$10 because I was at the Capitol on January 6th, and I didn't see an "insurrection." I saw Americans praying. Singing the national anthem. Waving flags. I saw families, veterans, and peaceful patriots standing up for what they believed in.

$10 because, since that day, I've watched in horror as men and women I stood with that day have been hunted down and treated like terroriSUPERLIST.

[$10 because even though J6ers have been pardoned, the pardons alone aren't enough.](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=c7b82e7143ac4dc894d403c92acdfd14&_e=db6bZeZW7KYkDA68vcaLauCxCErU85beDmh4kH_c9avwYf3Icwj1iMphXApg8p1IKzQFAfrld4zHCZSkREWl8qF5YnquWf3r288Lg_MHC5u8UFfoM1ignDx3sJetZAe8WsQG_kenw-1rpl4H3YcbULASp-II1o6x9iSCBfQv7a7xM6EwUm2FzUt-lVwqztI2LX7txQp4u9d_Y7cMYA_bVuuyYxNkkIuqT8XRGY4sAQ1hk06R0-ZMgpGeyJ9gmBSL9BgHBQfpmA0BNTpviVIK4OY-CVPTN5l5hL19D7VdyFqN-PSWAoI9ixo27nkKt0eAxnm4CQ1YhNWnnoOd3duYguJ6xYZXghpbC6TiippDQ8_HKnaFTSTtmnqNy9EkOzPszPhhFKMt_k2TjGyLqtslSAosgbSCq7fDV2EXqVrQQfFMwtr5ZfukSBKFf-8DeLXsnnqEwHPXGi62T86OLso_Rd5hZkn0hvVeyhtHZeqFLu8-NOqqBezIWZRR1RCxidNNv6RnaozbHJge_9HnY-j7hw6eoRzW-9VmNK3fb6hCEa0uHQQ13ezntETrsp2UbU_HwT9nbk8BCfOiYVTDfGiLOnV61Dsn3vDxLhOFARlXAEoU-MXJVHAsK5Z2c2Q1ETI-ketfcKUTZt3BcCduZFFL_g%3D%3D)

Hey folks,
The Andrew and Tristan Tate story somehow keeps getting stranger.
Their allies are blaming the DOJ, politicians, and basically anyone they can find as the brothers face possible extradition to the UK. I break down the latest arguments from Nick Fuentes, a bizarre conspiracy theory about Washington insiders, Joe McBride's return to the spotlight, and the increasingly contradictory messaging coming from the Tates' camp.
* [**00:00:23**] Andrew Tate says he'd rather spend months in jail than live like a "normal person" as the brothers continue fighting possible extradition to the UK.
* [**00:01:40**] Nick Fuentes weighs in on the Tate brothers' legal situation and argues that taking on the government is nearly impossible, which leads me into what's actually at stake in their court battles.
* [**00:04:13**] One of the Tates' allies offers a wild explanation for their legal problems, claiming powerful people in Washington targeted them after a private gathering.
* [**00:07:18**] Joe McBride resurfaces after going unusually quiet, and I break down his role in the public messaging surrounding the brothers versus the legal fight itself.
* [**00:09:18**] A new post attributed to Andrew Tate raises even more questions about the brothers' claims regarding their detention, and whether their own messaging is contradicting itself.

This episode is about more than the latest Tate drama. It's about the competing narratives surrounding their legal cases, the effort by their allies to portray them as victims of the system, and the very different question of what will actually happen when their allegations and defenses are tested in court. clean_body: | | | Across the Commonwealth | | ~~ WEEK WITHOUT DRIVING BEGINS TODAY! Join Bus Riders of Roanoke Advocacy Group and PedalSafe ROA as they kick off ~ so we can better understand the lives of non-drivers and support affordable, accessible transportation across Roanoke. By highlighting how there are people who lack access to driving in every community, Week Without Driving helps win policies that support access across both rural and urban communities -- and everywhere in between. MOONSHINE AND DEMOCRATS - Oct. 3 On Saturday, RCDC is hosting their Annual Fundraiser to help cover their costs and to help elect CD6 Congressional Candidate Beth Macy along with Roanoke City Council Candidates Vivian Sanchez-Jones, Danny Clawson and Raekwon Moore. Congressman James R. Walkinshaw representing Virginia's 11th Congressional District will be the guest speaker. CD6 Democratic Nominee Beth Macy will also be in attendance. | ~ | In the Community | | ENERGY COSTS LISTENING TOUR - ROANOKE RECAP Last week, Del. Rasoul joined Lt. Gov. Hashmi, Del. Franklin, and Mayor Cobb to discuss the NextEra/Dominion merger. The consensus is that this is a bad deal for Virginians. Enough is enough. This super-monopoly has no place in Virginia. Our energy bills are high enough. Now is not the time for anymore corporate greed. ~ | CELEBRATING PRIDE AT SWVA PRIDE FEST On Saturday, we celebrated five years of Southwest Virginia Pride! 🎉 The weekend's celebration was a beautiful display of unity and living a life authentically. Already looking forward to the next five years of this celebration! | HISPANIC HERITAGE MONTH LOCAL COLORS - Oct. 3 Join Local Colors for their 7th annual Hispanic Heritage Month Celebration this Saturday at the John Nolen Plaza from 12-4pm! This event is a free, family friendly celebration that spotlights the rich cultures of Latin America and recognizes the positive contributions of the Latino community in our area. It features dance and live music performances, educational segments, storytelling, and more. | SEMI- ANNUAL USED BOOK SALE - Oct. 3 The Semiannual Used Book Sale is back! Join community members at the Roanoke History Museum this Saturday for a one-day-only used book sale! Browse through over 1,000 titles--there will truly be something for everyone! | KOREAN FESTIVAL OF LETTERS: HANGUL DAY - Oct. 3 Join the Taubman Museum of Art for the 2026 Hangul Festival as they celebrate Korean language, culture, creativity, and community! Discover the beauty and history of Hangul (한글), the Korean alphabet, while experiencing Korean culture through an afternoon of interactive activities and entertainment. Bring your family and friends and celebrate the language and culture that connect Roanoke and our Sister City of Wonju, South Korea. | MOUNTAIN MAGIC IN FALL - Oct. 3 Join community members for Mountain Magic in Fall this Saturday, from 10 am -4 pm at the Buchanan Town Park! Celebrate the beauty of fall in Buchanan with local artisan vendors, delicious food trucks, a car show, live music and more. It's the perfect way to spend a day enjoying our mountain scenery and small-town charm. It will be a day full of fall fun, great food, unique shopping, and community! ~ | | | WAIT UNTIL 8TH WITH SAM RASOUL + RCC-PTA - Oct. 14 Join the community movement pledging not to give our children a smartphone until after 8th grade. Del. Sam Rasoul, Emily Harrison (Distraction Free Schools), Jessica Blandy (Roanoke City Council of PTAs/PTSAs), and Wesley Williams (RCPS Executive Director of Operations), will speak with community members about the benefits of not giving cell phones to children before they finish 8th grade. ~ | FREE VIRTUAL THERAPY AVAILABLE TO RCPS STUDENTS Through a partnership with Hazel Health, RCPS students can meet with a licensed therapist virtually for a therapy appointment at no cost to families. Sessions are available in multiple languages, and allow students to get help with anxiety, friendships, grief, big emotions, changes at school or home, and more. To request a therapy appointment for your student, call Hazel Health at 1-800-76-HAZEL (42935). ~~ | Community Resources | COMMUNITY OFFICE HOURS VIRTUAL OFFICE HOURS WITH DEL. RASOUL'S TEAM Our office is now holding virtual office hours to meet with constituents. Meet with a member of Delegate Sam Rasoul's team to ask questions, share concerns, or get help with state-related issues. We're here to listen and assist however we can. ~~ | | KNOW YOUR RIGHTS WITH ICE There have been recent reports of ICE throughout the state. The ACLU has created a collection of resources in the case you or someone you know interacts with ICE agents. Read and share the resources found ~~. ~~ | CONTACT YOUR FEDERAL REPRESENTATIVE In many ways, it feels like our federal government is under attack by the current administration. While our office is happy to assist however we can, it is still crucial that you engage our federal representatives. Find the contact information for the Virginia Congressional Delegation ~~. | JOIN THE ROANOKE CITY DEMOCRATS! RCDC's monthly business meeting is the third Thursday each month. Watch their Facebook for an upcoming announcement of the agenda. The meetings are available virtually for those who write to mailto:info@roanokedemocrats.com, requesting the link. ~~ | JOIN ROANOKE YOUNG DEMS! Meetings occur on the second Monday of every month in person and virtually. The goal of RYD is to help improve our community and to promote the names of Democratic candidates and policies. Contact: mailto:youngdemocratsroanoke@gmail.com to get involved! | BUILDING BELOVED COMMUNITIES Building Beloved Communities helps nonprofits and government agencies step into 2026 with clarity and confidence - whether it's bringing your annual report to life, guiding strategic planning, or supporting your team with resilience and leadership tools. ~~ | Thank you for your support! Beneath the sands and clays of Central Florida, deep within the limestone, another world moves unseen. The aquifer winds beneath us--a vast, hidden realm of water and stone, carrying what every well, tap, garden, and throat depends upon.
We walk above it without thought. The ground becomes a place to build, pave, plant, and pass over. Yet the ground is more than what holds us up. It holds what sustains us.
And what enters the ground does not simply disappear. It descends. It enters the veins of that hidden world. When the source is compromised, something more than water is lost. The sweetness of the ground begins to change.
**Pause.
Breathe.
