Photo by Halil Sagirkaya/Anadolu via Getty Images. A private intelligence firm working for the United Arab Emirates commissioned a report on American Muslim organizations from a U.S. researcher as part of a campaign aimed at damaging their reputations with allegations of links to the Muslim Brotherhood, according to an archive of leaked documents obtained by Drop Site News. The commission from the Geneva-based firm Alp Services resulted in a 2018 report produced by Lorenzo Vidino, the author of several books on the Muslim Brotherhood and head of the George Washington Program on Extremism at George Washington University. That report and other documents included in the archive lay out a proposed campaign against Muslim organizations in the United States, aspects of which appear to be ongoing. Titled "The MB in the US," Vidino's report lists the names of dozens of Muslim Americans and civil society groups that he claims are part of a vast and secretive extremist network in the U.S.--including the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR), the Islamic Society of North America (ISNA), the Muslim Public Affairs Council (MPAC), the Muslim American Society (MAS), the U.S. Council of Muslim Organizations, the charity Islamic Relief USA, along with several organizations, mosques, and individually named activists and religious leaders. The report does not provide evidence to substantiate Vidino's allegations. But it effectively created a blacklist of Muslim American organizations and individuals that could be used to damage their reputations with allegations of association with the Muslim Brotherhood, amid an ongoing effort pushed forward in part by the UAE to have the U.S. designate the group as a terrorist organization. Lorenzo Vidino and Alp Services did not respond to requests for comment. The UAE's Ministry of Foreign Affairs did not respond to questions. The broad effort to tie American Muslim groups to the Muslim Brotherhood has continued in the years since Vidino's report for Alp Services. On August 5, 2026, a Senate Judiciary subcommittee convened a titled "Hidden in Plain Sight: Confronting the Muslim Brotherhood Network in America." One of the three witnesses was Lara Burns, a senior research fellow at Vidino's Program on Extremism, who described CAIR, ISNA, the North American Islamic Trust and the Muslim Students Association as components of a covert Brotherhood and Hamas infrastructure, while citing Vidino's published work in portions of her written testimony. A Covert Defamation Campaign The UAE has been a major advocate of designating the Brotherhood as a terrorist group in Western countries after the organization won elections in several countries following the 2011 Arab Spring, leading to a perception that it was a threat to the power of the monarchy in Abu Dhabi. That campaign has gradually grown into a broader effort to target political rivals, or even individuals merely seen as suspicious or hostile by the Emirates. The documents contained in the archive, which was provided by the reporting consortium European Investigative Collaborations, reveal how the smear campaign was intended to come together. An internal Alp planning memo from July 2017 proposed creating, with Vidino's help, a "cartography" of alleged Muslim Brotherhood and Qatari influence networks in both the U.S. and Europe. That proposed map would encompass charities, lobbyists, media outlets, academics, political supporters, banks, investors, and businesspeople. Alp also contemplated deeper investigations intended to uncover what it called "red flags"--a reference to finding negative personal or professional information and rumors about selected targets. | | ---|---|--- This photograph taken on April 19, 2024 in Lausanne shows the logo of Geneva-based private intelligence company ALP Services. Photo by Fabrice Coffrini / AFP via Getty Images. In February 2018, Alp secured approval for an operation code-named "Arnica 6" that would ultimately turn some of the investigations into covert reputational and financial pressure campaigns. The action plan proposed hostile media placements, providing unattributed briefings to trusted journalists, negative Wikipedia editing about targets, submissions of derogatory information to regulatory compliance databases, and discreet political lobbying. Some details of Alp's European activities on behalf of the UAE were previously by the New Yorker, which described efforts to target a commodities trader named Hazim Nada, as well as Muslim organizations in Europe. The accusation of association with the Muslim Brotherhood, spread by Alp Services through anonymously posted online articles and Wikipedia entries, ruined Nada's business and reputation while generating millions of euros in revenue for the firm. The New Yorker noted that Mario Brero, the head of Alp Services, whose primary client on the project was an Emirati research institution reporting to UAE leader Mohammed bin Zayed, asked Vidino to find "'interesting elements/rumours' on the other side of the Atlantic," but did not provide specifics on any follow-up efforts to identify or target Americans or U.S.-based organizations. On May 12, 2018, Vidino transmitted a series of documents to Alp over WhatsApp, including his report on the Muslim Brotherhood in America and supporting memos on Muslim organizations in Chicago and groups linked to the Turkish government. The Brotherhood report was sent as a Microsoft Word file that includes metadata indicating that Vidino was the author. Other documents suggest that the proposed fee for producing this report was 2,000 euros. The report mapped a wide swath of Muslim American civic life, including registered, well-established organizations that he claimed comprised a covert Muslim Brotherhood network in America. Vidino did not provide evidence that the listed individuals or organizations were part of the Muslim Brotherhood or any other transnational organization, but asserted they were "spawns" of the movement and represented its "centers of gravity" in the United States. By July 2018, Alp had transformed Vidino's material into a polished report intended for its client, an Emirati entity called ARIAF Studies and Research LLC. Alp also assembled a separate package of documents for an August 8 meeting with Matar Humaid al-Neyadi, an Emirati official who appears elsewhere in the archive as the client contact for Arnica and currently serves as the UAE's ambassador to Kuwait. Al-Neyadi did not respond to a request for comment. | | ---|---|--- Lorenzo Vidino attends a press conference at Palazzo Chigi on January 5, 2017 in Rome, Italy, to explain the his research on radicalization. Photo by Camilla Morandi - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images. Targeting Civil Society Groups Prior to joining the GWU program, Vidino worked worked for the Investigative Project on Terrorism, a research organization founded by Steve Emerson, a controversial "terrorism expert" who has been accused of spying on American Muslim organizations and falsely claiming that major cities in Europe had become "no-go zones" under the control of Muslim immigrants. Vidino has remained influential as an expert commentator in the United States. In a Wall Street Journal op-ed in early August, Vidino that the Trump administration must begin targeting what he referred to as non-violent "Islamist" groups, claiming that such groups were already operating in "politics, education and grassroots activism," and that "Islamist actors are funding politically aligned candidates in U.S. elections nationwide." The article did provide any evidence for the claims or specify what it defined as "Islamist actors." A previous target of Vidino and Alp Services in Europe was an Austrian scholar now living in the U.S. named Farid Hafez. After rumors of his association with the Brotherhood were spread by Alp and later shared with Austria's intelligence services, Hafez's home was raided by Austrian police in November 2020. He was later cleared of any wrongdoing and the operations themselves were later found to be unlawful by Austrian courts. "Vidino never really says something specific like this person is a Muslim Brotherhood person, but instead uses the strategy of saying that those people have a relationship with other people who themselves have a relationship to the Brotherhood," said Hafez, who added that Vidino's reports predominantly relied on secondary sources. "There was never really a clear statement that someone could nail him down over in a courtroom, because he never really said anything too specific in his accusations, and that was really the strategy." Vidino's report for Alp claimed that despite having no visible organizational structure, the Muslim Brotherhood's American branch is "arguably one of the largest and best organized in the West," claiming that it had established itself with the arrival of Muslim college students to the country in the 1960s and has continued expanding its influence through a web of connected political, financial, and educational organizations. In addition to laying out the names and personnel associated with the largest and most well-known Muslim organizations in the U.S., the report also sets the stage for a broader possible crackdown on mosques in general by targeting an organization called the North American Islamic Trust, which holds the deeds to hundreds of American mosques. A short section devoted to charities also lists a number of charity organizations including Islamic Relief USA, the Zakat Foundation of America, Life for Relief and Development and Anera, a group that helps refugees in Palestine, Lebanon, and Jordan. Islamic Relief, a UK-headquartered charity that operates in disaster zones around the world, was also the target of a separate campaign funded by the UAE, code-named "Crocus," which was aimed at associating the organization with an American Muslim scholar named Yasir Qadhi, according to the documents. The documents in the archive from Alp related to the Crocus campaign cite a number of British press reports about Qadhi from 2017, quoting his past statements about Islamic criminal punishments, homosexuality, and Shia Muslims; describing him as a "radical preacher"; and noting that some of his social media posts had been shared by Islamic Relief employees. Qadhi had previously renounced some of his earlier views and has been defended by the charity as an opponent of terrorism. Islamic Relief has continued to be regularly targeted by social media campaigns led by UAE-backed online influencers. The report on American Muslims supplied by Vidino also included a section on alleged Turkish government influence in the U.S., including ties between Turkish officials and several American Muslim organizations and individuals. The Turkish government has also been a rival of the UAE in recent years after the two countries found themselves on opposite sides of the Arab Spring. American Muslim activists who were named by Vidino denied the accusations contained in the dossier, describing them as political attacks aimed at trying to exclude them from political life. "These are tactics that have been used against us for all these years to marginalize us and exclude us from politics. They are worried about losing their grip and monopolizing the American political scene," said Salam Al-Marayati, president and co-founder of the Muslim Public Affairs Council (MPAC). "If they can't win the argument--which they lose every time, particularly on foreign policy--their reaction is that these are wolves in sheep's clothing, this is a Trojan horse, we are the Muslim Brotherhood." Extremist Accusations For her August appearance before the Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing on the Muslim Brotherhood, Laura Burns submitted written testimony describing CAIR, ISNA, the North American Islamic Trust, and the Muslim Students Association as components of a covert Brotherhood and Hamas infrastructure. Another witness, Arielle Klepach of the National Jewish Advocacy Center, accused a still wider network that included CAIR, ICNA, ISNA, MAS, MSA and NAIT of being secret extremist groups and cited a series of Vidino's published reports. Klepach urged lawmakers to use financial and legal pressure against CAIR in particular, pointing to bills to strip the organization of its tax-exempt status, designate it as a terrorist organization, and investigate its alleged foreign ties. Other efforts to crack down on Muslim participation in American public life have included proposed legislation and executive orders. A bill called the Muslim Brotherhood Terrorist Designation Act, sponsored by Rep. Mario Diaz-Balart (R-Fla.) and Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) would require annual government reports identifying Brotherhood branches and evaluating them for terrorist designation and sanctions. A separate bill introduced by Rep. Chip Roy (R-Texas) would designate CAIR as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist Organization, freeze its assets, revoke its tax exemption and prohibit Americans from dealing with it. In November 2025, Trump signed an executive order directing the State and Treasury departments to the process of designating certain Muslim Brotherhood branches, including those in Egypt, Jordan, and Lebanon, as terrorist organizations. That same month, Texas Governor Greg Abbott issued a proclamation to designate both CAIR and the Muslim Brotherhood as foreign terrorist and transnational criminal organizations and said the designation would prohibit them and their alleged affiliates from acquiring land in Texas. Gov. Ron DeSantis on September 29 that Florida had officially designated the Muslim Brotherhood, CAIR, and "antifa" as terrorist organizations. These efforts have continued to be supported not only by pro-Israel organizations, but also Emirati officials who have pressed forward with an ambitious strategy of using their influence in the U.S. and Europe to wield terrorism accusations against their political rivals, using alleged ties to the Brotherhood as a preferred tactic. In January 2026, its foreign ministry welcomed the Trump administration's designation of Brotherhood branches in Egypt, Jordan, and Lebanon, while Roy's proposed legislation against CAIR explicitly cites the UAE's own 2014 designation of the organization. "The unfortunate fact is that the UAE has come to play a destabilizing role in the Middle East and in relation to Arab and Muslim communities in the West," said Osama Abu Irshaid, national director for American Muslims for Palestine, who is also named along with his organization in the Vidino and Alp documents. "They are not doing it because they truly believe we are an extension of the Muslim Brotherhood in the U.S. or EU, but because they feel that their interests are threatened, because we calling for freedom and liberty and are succeeding in our aspirations for integration, and they fear this may one day translate into foreign policy pressure on them to cease their repression across the the region." "There is nothing that would substantiate their claims. We are American organizations, we are American citizens, and we have the right to come together to organize politically. Everything we are doing is in public and there are no secrets," Irshaid added. Yesterday, we closed the books on our final end-of-quarter fundraising deadline before Election Day.
To everyone who chipped in, knocked on doors, talked with friends and neighbors or simply stayed up to date on this race: thank you. Every effort counts, and it's your support that will carry us through to the finish line.
I've spent my career fighting for North Carolinians, and I know that this race is different. At almost every event I attend, whether it's a canvass launch, a community meeting or a Make Stuff Cost Less event, someone comes up to me and tells me it's the first political event they've ever been to.
That gives me hope. People all across the state recognize that the swamp in Washington is deeper than ever, and these are not ordinary times. They are worried about the future of our state and country.
And folks aren't just ready to go to the polls and vote for change. They're signing up to canvass and talk with their neighbors, and they're telling me they're knocking doors for the first time. Making calls for the first time. Donating for the first time.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/1efc9039-de05-4a9e-ac03-31bd27b0d288?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
They're ready to show up.
I've said many times I'm a prisoner of hope. I truly believe our best days are ahead of us, if we work toward it. This campaign has shown me people are ready for a course correction, and they know that change is possible on November 3rd.
Thank you for being a part of this people-powered movement.
We have a lot of work to do in these last 5 weeks, and I'm grateful for everything you've done to get us here. We have 33 more days to keep showing up, keep talking with voters and finish this race strong.
[Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can spare to help us flip this crucial U.S. Senate seat and take back Washington? I can't do this without you.](https://substack.com/redirect/1efc9039-de05-4a9e-ac03-31bd27b0d288?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Yesterday's
judicial hearings were a sham — just like every other hearing we've seen
throughout Trump's second term.

Trump’s crony judicial nominees sat before the Senate and were asked a
simple question: Who won the 2020 election?

Again and again, they parroted a bizarre script approved by the White
House to protect Trump's big lie about losing in 2020.

Some nominees have even gone a step further and said that it’s
“inappropriate” to weigh in on a “disputed political matter.”

Congress, our election system, and investigation after investigation has
concluded the 2020 election is not disputed.

The only person disputing it is Trump. And his nominees — up for lifetime
seats on the federal bench — won't say the two words that might upset him:
"Biden won."

This is what Trump's second-term judiciary looks like: not judges who
interpret the law, but loyalists who protect his ego and his authoritarian
agenda. Rubber stamps for a man who can't admit he lost.

They say the American Dream dies in California. They tell you to flee the coasts, escape the high taxes and the regulation, and come to Tennessee. Come to the Volunteer State, where we don't tax your wages. Where we don't tax your retirement. Where the business climate is ranked in the top five in the nation, year after year. Where the budgets are balanced, the coffers are sober, and the politicians are "fiscally responsible."
It is quite a sales pitch, isn't it? Come to Tennessee! Keep more of what you earn! Build your business! Retire in comfort! And they are not wrong--not entirely. The State of Tennessee has done what so many governments refuse to do. Our constitution requires a balanced budget. We have resisted the siren song of a state income tax time and time again. We have kept corporate taxes low. Debt per capita remains among the lowest in the nation. Fiscal responsibility. It is not just a talking point here; it is the brand.

**The Origins of the Problem: Section 216 and the Federal Power Act**
Before 2005, electric transmission line siting was almost exclusively the province of individual states. Recognizing that this state-by-state patchwork was inadequate for the modern interconnected grid, Congress passed the Energy Policy Act of 2005 (EPAct 2005), which added Section 216 to the Federal Power Act (FPA). This provision created a limited, shared federal-state framework for siting interstate electric transmission facilities.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/05612216-2dfe-4814-8a75-02bf721933e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Under Section 216 as originally enacted, the Department of Energy (DOE) was authorized to study transmission congestion and designate "National Interest Electric Transmission Corridors" (NIETCs)--geographic areas experiencing significant transmission constraints. In those designated corridors, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) was granted "backstop" authority to issue permits for interstate transmission lines if states failed to act within one year or imposed conditions that did not substantially address the need. Crucially, Section 216(e) authorized permit holders to acquire necessary rights-of-way through federal eminent domain if they could not reach voluntary agreements with landowners.
However, this authority proved nearly unusable in practice. In a series of court decisions--most notably the Fourth Circuit's 2009 ruling in Piedmont Environmental Council v. FERC--federal courts interpreted Section 216 narrowly, holding that FERC lacked backstop authority where a state had affirmatively denied a transmission application. Since states could effectively block projects simply by saying "no," FERC's backstop power was rendered largely toothless. Between 2005 and 2021, virtually no major interstate transmission project was successfully sited using the Section 216 framework.
The 2021 Fix: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act
The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA)--signed into law by President Biden on November 15, 2021 (P.L. 117-58)--was popularly understood as a "$1.2 trillion roads and bridges package." Buried within its provisions, however, was a critically important set of amendments to Section 216 of the FPA that essentially resuscitated and expanded FERC's dormant backstop siting authority.
**The IIJA amendments accomplished four key things** :
First, Congress explicitly overrode the Piedmont decision's interpretation. The amended statute now makes clear that FERC may exercise its backstop permitting authority when a state has affirmatively denied a siting application--not merely when a state fails to act within the one-year window. This is the restoration of the backstop power that the courts had stripped away.
Second, the amendments expanded the circumstances under which DOE may designate National Corridors, broadening the geographic scope where FERC's authority applies.
Third, the IIJA retained the eminent domain power under Section 216(e) but added a "good faith engagement" requirement. FERC must now determine that a permit holder has made genuine, early efforts to engage with landowners and stakeholders before that holder may exercise eminent domain authority to acquire land.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0f199da9-b0a7-492d-9fe5-fb86b9a9c6ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Fourth, the amendments clarified and preserved FERC's authority in ways that make the process more predictable for developers seeking to build major interstate transmission projects.
**The Connection to Data Centers Today**
While the IIJA's Section 216 amendments were not written with data centers specifically in mind, they laid essential legal groundwork for the massive transmission buildout that is now enabling the data center boom.
America's data center industry--particularly hyperscale cloud and AI facilities--has experienced explosive growth. A single modern AI training facility can consume as much electricity as a small city, and developers have been building campuses containing multiple such facilities across Virginia, Texas, Arizona, Ohio, and other states. Regional grids that lacked sufficient transmission capacity to serve this demand faced a fundamental constraint: electrons cannot be transmitted without wires, and crossing state lines historically meant navigating a maze of incompatible permitting regimes.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e796037e-25e6-43f9-8cb3-839c7ee56134?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
By reviving FERC's backstop authority, the IIJA created a federal pathway for building the large-scale, interstate, high-voltage transmission lines that connect remote generation resources (especially renewable energy in rural areas and offshore wind on the coasts) to the metropolitan and exurban locations where data centers are proliferating. Transmission developers can now pursue federal permits with eminent domain authority when states erect barriers, allowing the grid to expand to meet demand that has grown far beyond what any single state can address on its own.
In this sense, the IIJA's Section 216 amendments were a prerequisite condition for the physical infrastructure that supports the modern digital economy. Without robust transmission, there is no reliable power; without reliable power, there are no data centers to train the large language models, stream the content, and store the data that define contemporary life.
**Who Were the Congressional Sponsors?**
The IIJA's passage required bipartisan cooperation in an era of deep partisan polarization. The bill's legislative history involved two distinct groups: the **Senate bipartisan negotiators** who crafted the overall framework, and the **House sponsors** who advanced the specific vehicle that became law.
House Leadership:
The formal House vehicle was H.R. 3684, introduced by Representative Peter DeFazio (D-OR), then-Chairman of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure. DeFazio, a longtime champion of federal infrastructure investment, was the named sponsor in the House. The Senate took up the House bill, substituted its negotiated text, and passed it first before returning it to the House for final passage.
The Senate Bipartisan Working Group:
The breakthrough came from a bipartisan group of senators--sometimes called the "G10" or the "G20" as it expanded--who negotiated the package directly with the White House. The two leaders of this effort were:
\- Senator Rob Portman (R-OH) - The Ohio Republican was the lead Republican negotiator and arguably the most visible GOP advocate for the package.
\- Senator Kyrsten Sinema (D-AZ) - The Arizona Democrat was the lead Democratic negotiator alongside Portman and was instrumental in keeping the talks alive.
The core bipartisan group of senators who announced the initial framework included:
\- Bill Cassidy (R-LA)
\- Susan Collins (R-ME)
\- Joe Manchin (D-WV)
\- Lisa Murkowski (R-AK)
\- Mitt Romney (R-UT)
\- Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH)
\- Jon Tester (D-MT)
\- Mark Warner (D-VA)
This group swelled to roughly 20 senators in total as the negotiations proceeded, eventually producing a bill that passed the Senate 69-30 on August 10, 2021. The House then passed the amended bill 228-206 on November 5, 2021, and President Biden signed it into law ten days later.
The use of eminent domain to stop a lawful development sets a dangerous precedent, and nowhere is that clearer than in Nashville today. Mayor Freddie O'Connell's decision to seize private property largely to block a DC BLOX data center near the Nashville Zoo deserves scrutiny, because it treats condemnation not as a tool of last resort for genuine public works, but as a political veto on private enterprise.
Eminent domain is constitutionally reserved for "public use." Traditionally, that has meant roads, schools, utility corridors, and projects that serve the public and that genuinely require public ownership. Claiming the need for office space might satisfy the letter of state enabling statutes, but the timing of this condemnation is impossible to ignore. Metro is simultaneously pursuing a data center moratorium and aggressive zoning restrictions. To suddenly discover that the exact parcel a data center developer wants must be seized by the city reveals a motive that looks pretextual.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/74370bd9-d6c9-4476-aaaf-831d1dc975c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The practical danger is straightforward enough. If Nashville can seize land because it dislikes a particular industry, other cities will notice. Companies looking to invest billions in infrastructure--often projects that bring significant tax revenue and construction jobs--will factor in the risk that a mayor can simply take the land if politics demand it. That unpredictability chills investment not just in data centers, but in any capital-intensive project that requires long-term certainty.
There is also an awkward contradiction in the policy. Cities across Tennessee and the broader region are actively courting data centers for their economic benefits. Nashville's objection appears rooted partly in neighborhood aesthetics and traffic concerns--legitimate topics for zoning and negotiation--but not for expropriation. If the concern is proximity to the zoo, address it through ordinary land-use authority, setbacks, or negotiated mitigation. If the concern is coding and zoning, rewrite the code. What Metro is doing instead is reaching for one of the most aggressive powers government possesses to ensure that a specific disfavored project simply never happens.
Above all, the precedent cuts both ways. If a mayor can deploy eminent domain to block a data center, another mayor could deploy it to force one in, or to override local objection to any other facility. Condemnation should be a narrow exception, not a flexible political instrument. Nashville's Metro Council may have wrapped this in the language of "office space," but the signal it sends is unmistakable: your property rights extend only as far as the current administration's development preferences allow. Businesses, landowners, and the courts should push back hard before that standard becomes normal.
**Conclusion**
The IIJA's amendments to Section 216 of the Federal Power Act represent one of the most consequential but underreported provisions in the 2021 infrastructure law. By reversing court decisions that had neutered FERC's authority, Congress restored a federal mechanism for siting interstate transmission lines and preserved the power of eminent domain for private developers acting within designated National Corridors. This authority is now being called upon to build the transmission infrastructure necessary to serve a data center economy whose electricity appetite has grown exponentially--connecting generation to load across state lines in ways that individual state regulators could not reliably achieve alone.

Neither group would even look their constituents in the eye or engage with their proposals. Commissioners in Texas wouldn't even raise their heads when asked, their minds made up for their partisan mission. In North Carolina, the Election Board Chairman threatened to call the cops on students if they didn’t leave. Voter suppression isn't just black-and-white photos of eligible voters being turned away from polling places. Voter suppression is making it harder for eligible voters to take part in our elections through onerous ID requirements, closing polling places, taking away voting locations, or ending mail-in voting. Every time someone makes it harder to cast your ballot, voters are suppressed.** = | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country. Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities. = = Contributions or gifts to Integrity First Voter Action Project are not tax deductible as charitable contributions or as business expenses under IRC Section 162(3). Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army.
During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. **Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. **
**I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and _I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud._**

clean_body: I’m a combat veteran and a father. I hope you will read this.| | | | | Peter, it’s John James. I wanted to introduce myself. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. I promise I will not waste your time. I just want to tell you a little about myself; it’s about time we got well-acquainted. I was born and raised in Michigan, and throughout high school, I felt a deep-rooted call to service. I decided I wouldn’t just read about service in the magazines, I would live it. Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army. During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud. After coming back stateside, I swapped my fatigues for a suit. I took over the family business, creating jobs here in Michigan and earning a master’s in supply chain management from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Michigan. I was never one to rest, and after making so many life-or-death decisions in Iraq, I knew every second mattered; I wanted to make the most of my time for my family and me. I never for a second considered running for office, and the last thing I’d consider myself is a politician... I saw the Democrats destroying our country, and I knew my service to this great nation wasn’t over yet. Everybody told me running for office isn’t easy, but my heart was telling me it was the right thing to do. I won my election, with the help of President Trump, and started delivering results for my new constituents. Then, in 2023, when the Establishment tried to move on from Trump and being MAGA was seen as risky or politically inconvenient, I was among the first in Michigan to endorse President Trump for 2024. Loyalty isn’t a talking point to me; it’s the only way I know how to operate. My dedication to this country, my loyalty towards my constituents, and my desire to see the greatest nation on earth excel are part of the reasons why I’m now emailing you, but they’re not my #1 reason why... These three kids are the reason why I’m sending this message to you, as a Republican and father running to be the next governor of Michigan Having my own family taught me more lessons than I could list, and it was the one thing being in the U.S. Army didn’t prepare me for. But it also awoke in me a desire to do EVERYTHING and ANYTHING I can to ensure my kids have bright futures. My family means everything to me, and Michigan is our home; that’s why I will fight like my life depends on it to save this state and win this November. I’m under no illusions; I know this election will be one of the toughest challenges I’ve faced in my entire life, but after everything I’ve done in my service, it’s nothing I can’t handle. Unfortunately, the one thing I can’t directly control is spending, and the Democrats will do everything in their power to stop my campaign from making it to the ballot box this November. Nothing can stop us from saving this country if we stand together. Today, I’m asking you to make a small-dollar gift of $10, $25, $50 or ANYTHING you can spare to fuel my campaign’s fight as we approach our upcoming November 3rd election. Thank you for taking the time to read my message. I hope to hear from you in the days to come. subject: Petition: Protect the Kennedy Center
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Schiff for Senate
body:
| If the President can't put his name on it, he is willing to close it or destroy it.
---
[](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/8022?amount=10&t=1&refcode=aschiff_email_100126_kennedycenterpetition&akid=10626%2E5257348%2E-FR8kz)
Derek, Donald Trump would rather shut down the Kennedy Center than let it stand without his name on it. It's not just absurd. It's destructive of a great cultural institution— and absurd — the president of the United States, spending his time and energy scheming over whether his name goes on a memorial named for an assassinated president, while one of the nation's great cultural institutions sits closed because of it. _If the President can't put his name on it, he is willing to close it or destroy it._ He cares more about branding our institutions in his image than he does preserving them for all of us. Congress allocated $257 million to repair the Kennedy Center. It should insist that work be done properly — not held hostage until Trump's name goes back on the building. Congress could stop this in a heartbeat if it wanted to. My colleagues have pushed for bipartisan legislation — Democrats and Republicans together — to protect the Kennedy Center, and memorials like it, from being torn down without Congress's consent. **[_Will you add your name in support of this fight to protect the Kennedy Center and stop Trump from treating our institutions like his personal property?_](https://act.adamschiff.com/signup/aschiff_email_100126_kennedycenterpetition?t=10&refcode=aschiff_email_100126_kennedycenterpetition&akid=10626%2E5257348%2E-FR8kz)** | | [ADD YOUR NAME→](https://act.adamschiff.com/signup/aschiff_email_100126_kennedycenterpetition?t=11&refcode=aschiff_email_100126_kennedycenterpetition&akid=10626%2E5257348%2E-FR8kz)

| Friend, In the past few weeks, MAGA has unleashed a blitzkrieg in the courts. Two decisions in particular should send a chill down every American's spine. The Supreme Court ruled that Alabama can suspend an ongoing election to rush through a gerrymandered map. This came after the same court threw out a challenge to Texas' illegal racially gerrymandered maps — ruling it was too close to an election for the courts to intervene. That Texas decision came in December. Months before the primary. In Virginia, the MAGA-packed state Supreme Court went even further — overruling the results of a statewide redistricting referendum where millions of voters went to the polls and a majority said yes. Read that again. A court overruled the results of an election.

His United States Senate race in Texas is FAR TOO CLOSE , and we have an urgent situation now. We can't lose Texas to the Democrats. Period. Ted Cruz | From: Ken Paxton <ken@kenpaxton.com> | | | Fellow Patriot, Back in 2018, when progressive Democrat Beto O'Rourke challenged Ted Cruz for Senate in Texas, Senator Cruz was leading by 3 points at this stage of the race. Today? James Talarico leads me by an average of just 2.6% in recent polling. This is shocking, and it should be a huge wake-up call to every America First patriot in the country - because as Ted Cruz recently reminded us all: If we lose Texas, we lose the country, and Democrats will use their power in Washington to CRUSH us! Democrats want to throw open the border, dismantle ICE, defund law enforcement, raise our taxes, while allowing violent criminals back on the streets... They want to pack the Supreme Court and to force the transgender agenda on our kids. The Democrats are dangerous. So, please don 't sit this race out... I need YOUR help, Fellow Patriot. You can imagine how people in Washington, D.C. react to that insulting, irresponsible language. Thankfully, I am working to make sure that our federal aid request is on track.(In addition to beheading DHS, Conroy also proposed a bizarre plan – and I’m not making this up – to empty illegal immigrant detention centers so illegal aliens could help fund Social Security, saying illegals “...all contribute to it.”)That isn't a minor policy disagreement. And it isn't something voters should have to discover by watching an old clip after being told it never happened.[Carmela said it. The tape shows it.](https://us.list-manage.com/iZVAK7bZGf8?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)I walked out of our last debate just shaking my head. Where does she get these ideas? subject: Sacramento just targeted me — and only me
body:
Must read

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/f8pmj7VIOil?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)
| |

Friends,

**Governor Newsom just signed SB 1379.**
This bill was authored by DSA State Sen. Sabrina Cervantes. Now she and Sacramento have used state power to strip me of an office the voters of Riverside County elected me to serve.
I was elected Sheriff and public Coroner. That is how 48 of California’s 58 counties still operate. One person. One department. Local control.SB 1379 does not apply to those other 57 counties. It targets Riverside County. **It targets me**.
---
| | | | | [Support Bianco](https://us.list-manage.com/E4XGstGcNgV?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)
---
| |
The Democrat-majority Board of Supervisors now has to appoint a separate official and stand up an entirely new department — staff, building, bureaucracy — while the county is already staring at a nearly $70 million deficit. Taxpayers will pay for a political hit job.This is not reform. **This is political weaponization**.
The same Democrat supervisors already shorted my department by $125 million. That is not “oversight.” **This is defund the police**.
Look at the pattern.They defunded the Sheriff’s Office. They passed a law to stop sheriffs from examining ballots that are the subject of a criminal investigation. The California Supreme Court then piled on. Now they carve the Coroner’s Office away from the only county they decided to single out.
This is what one-party rule looks like when it cannot beat you at the ballot box: change the rules. Isolate one official.
**Stand with me. Contribute what you can. Help me fight this.**

Sheriff Chad Bianco
Riverside County
---

clean_body: Must read | | | | | | | Friends, Governor Newsom just signed SB 1379. This bill was authored by DSA State Sen. Sabrina Cervantes. Now she and Sacramento have used state power to strip me of an office the voters of Riverside County elected me to serve. I was elected Sheriff and public Coroner. That is how 48 of California’s 58 counties still operate. One person. One department. Local control.SB 1379 does not apply to those other 57 counties. It targets Riverside County. It targets me. | | | | | | | The Democrat-majority Board of Supervisors now has to appoint a separate official and stand up an entirely new department — staff, building, bureaucracy — while the county is already staring at a nearly $70 million deficit. Taxpayers will pay for a political hit job.This is not reform. This is political weaponization. The same Democrat supervisors already shorted my department by $125 million. That is not “oversight.” This is defund the police. Look at the pattern.They defunded the Sheriff’s Office. They passed a law to stop sheriffs from examining ballots that are the subject of a criminal investigation. The California Supreme Court then piled on. Now they carve the Coroner’s Office away from the only county they decided to single out. This is what one-party rule looks like when it cannot beat you at the ballot box: change the rules. Isolate one official. Stand with me. Contribute what you can. Help me fight this. Sheriff Chad Bianco Riverside County | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Our mailing address is: 17130 Van Buren Blvd Riverside, CA 92504 Want to change how you receive these emails? body:
Insulin costs. Alzheimer's research. Maine values. Will you stand with me?

Insulin costs. Alzheimer's research. Maine values. Will you stand with me?
| [](https://trk.email.goprelease.-8LXl1Ug)
---
Peter,I grew up in Aroostook County, Maine - as far north as you can go and still be in the continuous United States. It's a place where people work with their hands, look out for their neighbors, and don't expect anyone to hand them anything.That's the Maine I carry with me every single day in Washington.It's why, when I became Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, one of the most powerful posts in the entire Senate, I didn't forget where I came from. I use that gavel to fight for the things that actually matter to families like the ones I grew up with:
---
* Capping the cost of insulin so no Mainer living with diabetes has to choose between medication and groceries.
* Fighting for real funding for Alzheimer's research, because I've seen what this disease does to families, and I refuse to look away.
* Delivering for our veterans, our farmers, our fishermen, and our small towns that Washington so often forgets.

---
I didn't take the easy path to get here, and I'm not taking the easy path now. But I can't do this alone.Maine gave me everything. Now I need you to stand up for Maine.[Can I count on you to please chip in today and help me keep fighting for the people who raised me?](https://trk.email.goprelease._tfhyhoU3W1Vw7FHM4OQ)

Thank you,

Susan

It's now October, which means spooky season has officially begun.
And recent polls have MAGA's ghouls running scared all across the country, as an unprecedented blue tsunami chases in their wake:

---
However, there is one spine-chilling scenario for Democrats.
One where we take back the Senate and House....but quietly lose critical state Supreme Court races down ballot.
Michigan, Montana, and North Carolina all have state Supreme Court elections with massive implications:

* In Michigan, two liberal justices are fighting for their lives to stay on the court. A loss here would pave a path for MAGA to take back the court in coming years.

* In Montana, progressives are attempting to keep their majority on the court in what is considered a deep red state. If MAGA wins, the court flips.

* In North Carolina, Democrats are defending Justice Earls' seat. A win for Democrats here sets up an opportunity to flip the court entirely in 2028.

Losing these races would be so devastating that it could haunt the party for decades.
To make matters scarier, the high-profile Senate and House races are hogging the headlines and the endless TV ads, and these Supreme Court candidates might as well be ghosts.
That is where Defend Our Courts comes in. In the final, frightening stretch of the midterms, we are shining a flashlight into the dark corners of the ballot. We are putting a spotlight on these races and contacting Democratic voters so they know exactly who to vote for.
We have scared off MAGA's court takeovers before. In 2025, we spearheaded the defense of Pennsylvania's Supreme Court. With the help of over 100,000 Democrats nationwide, Pennsylvania's liberal justices kept their majority by landslide margins. We did it again in Wisconsin earlier this year and helped deliver another blowout that sent MAGA running for the exits.

Peter,

Angry Leftists tried for two years to**EXCUSE Luigi Mangione 's political violence... **to claim he was "fighting corporate greed" and some kind of "American hero."

You and I always knew what he was, and now he's admitted it:

_**He 's nothing more than a cold-blooded killer.**_

Last month, Mangione stood up in federal court and told the truth. He pleaded guilty to stalking Brian Thompson. He admitted, in his own words, that he shot him and that Thompson died. He now faces life in prison.

Brian Thompson was a husband and a father of two. The man was gunned down on a Manhattan sidewalk for the crime of running a successful company.

But here's the issue, Peter:

**The radical collectivist ideology that bent over backwards to LIONIZE him for being a violent murderer is still VERY much alive.**

Because that's what these dehumanizing ideologues teach young people: that it's somehow **_MORAL_ to violently punish someone simply for being successful.**

I'm Jennifer Anju Grossman, CEO of The Atlas Society. Ayn Rand spent her life warning the West what happens when a culture stops honoring achievement and starts resenting it.

She had a name for what drives someone to cheer a murderer because the victim was successful: envy, "the hatred of the good for being good."

Ayn Rand offered a radical alternative: that **achievement is not a crime...** and **political disagreement is NOT an excuse** to commit violence.

At the Atlas Society, **we 're fighting to reach young people BEFORE their resentments curdle into radicalism and violence.**

[We need your help to continue reaching them — and to take the MORAL case for individualism and achievement to the next generation. Every $10 we raise helps us reach 2,000 young minds.

Engage young people with Ayn Rand's fierce advocacy for reason, individualism, and freedom to INSPIRE the next generation.

clean_body: Peter, Angry Leftists tried for two years toEXCUSE Luigi Mangione 's political violence... to claim he was "fighting corporate greed" and some kind of "American hero." You and I always knew what he was, and now he's admitted it: He 's nothing more than a cold-blooded killer. Last month, Mangione stood up in federal court and told the truth. He pleaded guilty to stalking Brian Thompson. He admitted, in his own words, that he shot him and that Thompson died. He now faces life in prison. Brian Thompson was a husband and a father of two. The man was gunned down on a Manhattan sidewalk for the crime of running a successful company. But here's the issue, Peter: The radical collectivist ideology that bent over backwards to LIONIZE him for being a violent murderer is still VERY much alive. Because that's what these dehumanizing ideologues teach young people: that it's somehow MORAL to violently punish someone simply for being successful. I'm Jennifer Anju Grossman, CEO of The Atlas Society. Ayn Rand spent her life warning the West what happens when a culture stops honoring achievement and starts resenting it. She had a name for what drives someone to cheer a murderer because the victim was successful: envy, "the hatred of the good for being good." Ayn Rand offered a radical alternative: that achievement is not a crime... and political disagreement is NOT an excuse to commit violence. At the Atlas Society, we 're fighting to reach young people BEFORE their resentments curdle into radicalism and violence. Ayn Rand's warning explains a lot about where we are right now. A majority of young Americans tell pollsters they view socialism favorably. Campus departments teach that wealth is theft. Somewhere between the seminar and the comment section, murdering a CEO turned into a talking point instead of a horror. The Atlas Society exists to interrupt that. The Atlas Society's mission is simple: Engage young people with Ayn Rand's fierce advocacy for reason, individualism, and freedom to INSPIRE the next generation. Unlike the collectivists, we don't tell students how to think or what they must believe. We just supply the facts, and let them interpret and decide for themselves: We HOST wonderful programs like our 22 John Galt Schools to give young adults a forum to think critically about the world around them, We BUILD content designed to go viral and inspire students -- Draw My Life videos, graphic novels, anything that can translate Ayn Rand's ideas into the content they're already consuming, We HOST two annual student conferences -- Galt's Gulch and the New Intellectuals Conference --** joining together the next generation of freedom fighters. For years, too many stood idly by as the radical collectivists ran roughshod over our schools, our universities, our media, our society. Too many assumed that surely reason would prevail, but let me tell you, Peter: Reason must be taught. Respect for individuals must be learned. Violence must be discouraged. Wisdom must be accumulated. But it's not too late. The Atlas Society is fighting back HARD. Thank you, Jennifer Anju Grossman (JAG) CEO, The Atlas Society The Atlas Society is a 501(c)(3) Not For Profit Organization. All donations are tax-deductible.

TODAY'S TOP STORIES

COLORADO HOMEBUILDING FEES: SAME HOUSE, $77,000 APART
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

In Thornton, the water and sewer charges alone on a new
2,000-square-foot house come to $57,203. Add the rest of the taxes and
fees, and the total reaches $79,503, according to a new report from
the Common Sense Institute (CSI).

Somebody pays it. Depending on the market, the report says, that kind
of cost is absorbed through a lower price for the land, a smaller
return for the builder or a higher price for the buyer. Or the house
never gets built.

The Sept. 23 report priced the same hypothetical house, on the same
7,000-square-foot lot, in 16 Colorado cities. Taxes and fees ranged
from $24,295 in Colorado Springs to $101,616 in Boulder. That is a gap
of more than $77,000 on an identical home.

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

A COACH’S PERSPECTIVE: PROP 134 PROTECTS GIRLS WHO ARE AFRAID TO
JOIN
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY ROBERT SENCENBAUGH, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_A former coach argues the biggest barrier keeping girls out of sports
isn't skill, it's fear, and Prop 134 addresses one source of that fear
directly._

*
GETTING GIRLS TO JOIN WAS THE REAL CHALLENGE: The author writes that
teaching skills was never the hard part of coaching. Getting hesitant
girls, many trying organized sports for the first time, to sign up at
all was, with over 95% motivated by teamwork and friendship rather
than competition.

*
A SPECIFIC, NAMED FEAR: He identifies girls' reluctance to compete
against male students as a current barrier keeping some from starting
sports at all, framing Prop 134 as addressing both physical and
emotional safety concerns.

*
SAFETY AS THE DECIDING TENET: Drawing on his classroom rule that
physical and emotional safety come first, the author argues passing
the measure protects the benefits sports provide to girls' health,
confidence, and education, rather than risking losing them before they
start.

80 miles from Mexico City, where my aunt, a Catholic missionary nun,
had a convent and school. I saw desperate poverty and subsistence
living and zero government investment._

obtained for each to put these issues on the ballot for Coloradans to

People ask me all the time why I left the Republican Party. They expect a simple answer. A single moment. A breaking point. There wasn't one. There were _hundreds._ I grew up believing the GOP stood for something. Fiscal discipline. Strong institutions. A belief that character counted, that the office was bigger than the man who held it. That's the party my parents raised me to respect.That party is gone. What's left is a party that no longer asks whether something is true, only whether it's loyal. A party where senators who once criticized Donald Trump in private now defend him in public because they're afraid of a primary. A party that has traded the Constitution for a cult of personality. I sat in rooms with these people. I watched the transformation happen in real time — principle by principle, surrender by surrender. This is not the party of my father, who believed in hard work and honest leaders. It is not even the party it was ten years ago. **It is Donald Trump's party now, full stop. And it is up to us to stop it from doing any more damage to this country.** That's why Resist Reclaim Rebuild is fighting in the districts where this fight will actually be decided — the battlegrounds where a MAGA rubber stamp can be replaced by someone who still believes in checks and balances. **[Will you chip in $10, $25 or whatever you can today to help Resist Reclaim Rebuild take back these seats?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140452313/650535344/-323302678?refcode=261001_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTg3NGEyNzMtZDdiZC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=L-2OSNNkWRcdS36yg3NvDVFFDXiQiNhbe-f_c6r_ztc=)**

# **Micron 's 87% margin is a blessing the tape won't pay for**
Micron just printed a fantasy quarter and the tape yawned. Fiscal Q4 revenue $54.23 billion, up 379% from $11.32 billion. Non-Generally Accepted Accounting Principles Earnings per Share $33.42 versus $31.61 expected. Gross margin 87%. Up more than 500% in a year, the stock near $1,071 barely moved. The crowd already got paid. It is pricing the hangover.
* **Winners?** Micron and the HBM longs. DRAM hit $39.8 billion, up 343%, and more than 75% of fiscal 2027 output is already committed. Mehrotra says 2027 and 2028 only get tighter.
* **Losers?** Late money that wanted a gap after a 500% year. An 87% margin blesses you until the cycle remembers gravity. The curse is duration, not this beat.
* **Next?** Murphy has no line of sight on the shortage ending. Q1 guide is $61.5 billion and $38.15 a share. Cash return steps up December 9. The $2.2 billion buyback left is the appetizer next to Nvidia's $235 billion.

I crowned this[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/71555c38-1def-46c0-aeb6-2b24190645a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[the next Nvidia on July 1](https://substack.com/redirect/71555c38-1def-46c0-aeb6-2b24190645a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in " and told you to buy it with both fists. The **[July 8 carnage piece](https://substack.com/redirect/cbc196a5-0c1e-4480-80ec-2bbe1ff495ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** said memory was the bottleneck. It still is. Cash sits at $73.5 billion. Free cash flow was $62.3 billion. Fabs do not land by Christmas. Stay long the shortage. Trade the yawn.

# **Gemini 4 is a model drop in a personal agent market**
Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon on September 30 with coding and cyber gains, tying OpenAI on a key security test, priced to match GPT-6.1 Sol at $2 and $10 per million tokens. Wall Street did not ask about the benchmark. JPMorgan wants a personal agent people actually open. Spark stays behind the paywall. Meta's Muse is free, racking up millions of downloads, and already took the App Store from ChatGPT. Alphabet is down about 6% in three months. Meta is up 19%.
* **Winners?** Meta, which shipped a free agent and took the habit, and cloud buyers who will rent Argon for code without caring about the brand war.
* **Losers?** Google's consumer AI story, and any analyst still grading this race on model cards instead of the app people open daily.
* **Next?** Another capex quarter, another model, and a personal-agent gap Muse keeps widening until Sundar puts Spark in front of the paywall.

# **SpaceX just sold Google a ride to a science-project data center**
Data Centers in Space are here. Thursday's Transporter-18 Falcon 9 out of Vandenberg lifted a Planet Labs fridge with four Google TPUs in to space. Project Suncatcher. About a kilowatt of solar, fifteen minutes of compute at a time, 130 payloads on the stack, booster on its 25th flight. Pathfinder for radiation and heat, pulled forward from a 2027 twin-sat plan. Deutsche Bank's math: a gigawatt in orbit runs about 6 times a ground build ex-compute today, maybe 1 to 1.5 times by decade's end, cheaper only in the early 2030s if Starship actually flies the cost out.
* **Winners?** SpaceX, which gets paid to loft the experiment and keeps the cadence, and Google if low-earth-orbit power ever beats a terrestrial interconnect queue.
* **Losers?** Anyone modeling orbital AI as a 2026 revenue line, and the power-politics crowd that thought the constraint was permanent.
* **Next?** Radiation and thermal data, then a constellation pitch. The economics stay a lab note until the kilowatts stop looking like a hair dryer.

# **Hegseth just put the vendors on the war board**
At Quantico on September 30, Hegseth stood up Project Meridian and named Elon Musk, Anduril's Palmer Luckey, and Newt Gingrich as co-leads. One hundred twenty days. Report due January 28, 2027. The brief runs from under the earth to beyond the moon. Same speech: Autonomous Warfare Command, a four-star drone outfit with service-like authorities, targeted for October 1, 2027.
* **Winners?** SpaceX and Anduril, now inside the requirements process instead of bidding against a slide deck written in 2014.
* **Losers?** Legacy primes still selling manned platforms into an autonomous budget, and any staff officer who thought Silicon Valley was a vendor.
* **Next?** A January report that reads like a shopping list. Autonomy, power, and space. Then the purchase orders.

The Pentagon is the new hyperscaler checkbook, same tape as the[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/af2d75a5-5ba3-46d6-b3cc-5548bdef16b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[September 18 Fluidstack loan talks.](https://substack.com/redirect/af2d75a5-5ba3-46d6-b3cc-5548bdef16b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Musk does not need a study to know what he will sell them. # **Optical names just got paid for the pipe under the GPUs**

Coherent's PhotonLink packages lasers, fiber, and detectors for the data center, with about 20 customer engagements across co-packaged and near-packaged optics, plus five in chip-to-chip. **Join us for the Meet the Candidates Cocktail Reception** to open the night, followed by an Intimate Dinner with our V.I. Senate Candidates. A special evening bringing together supporters and the candidates working to restore real competition and accountability to the Virgin Islands Government.

The reception is hosted by RPVI Chairman John Yob, Francie Whitenburg, Jim Hughes,
and Dr. Alexandria Coronado Hughes.

There are two ways to join us: come for the CocktailReception, or reserve a Dinner ticket, which includes the Cocktail Reception, for thefull evening.
**
Event Details
Monday, October 12
**
**Cocktail Reception:** 5:30 – 6:30 PM
An hour of cocktails and mingling with fellow supporters, connecting with old and new friends and neighbors from across the islands. Meet and greet with the candidates who are stepping up to serve the people of the VI face-to-face.
**Cocktail Reception ticket:** $50
---
| [COCKTIAL RECEPTION TICKETS](https://us.list-manage.com/Bcr3YGeGNfk?e=4f81ceec6f&c2id=39a671a1d75d16cde42206c3cb925b2d)
---
| |

**Intimate Dinner with VI Senate Candidates:** 6:30 PM
After the cocktail reception, the evening continues with an intimate seated dinner with the Senate candidates from across the VI. Sit down with Raymond, Eric, and Derrick. Hear their vision for the islands up close, ask the questions that matter to you, and share a memorable evening over delicious food and great company.
**Dinner Tickets** : $500
---
| [DINNER TICKETS](https://us.list-manage.com/OUIiK6hSxGT?e=4f81ceec6f&c2id=39a671a1d75d16cde42206c3cb925b2d)
---
| |

**Meet the Candidates
Raymond T. James, Esq**. (St. Croix District)A lifelong Virgin Islander and small businessman who served as Assistant Attorney General,Raymond has spent his career fighting for the people of these islands. He's running to bringreal accountability, integrity, and a clear-eyed vision back to Virgin Islands government.

**Eric Tillett** (St. Thomas & St. John District)A builder, not a career politician. Eric is ready to restructure WAPA, modernize the grid, anddrive down electric rates — while growing a digital economy so our islands are no longerdependent on tourism alone.

**Derrick Callwood**(St. Thomas & St. John District)Shaped by years in community organizing and law enforcement, Derrick knows what islandfamilies need: better roads, reliable power, affordable housing, and stronger public schools.He's running to deliver all four.

Tickets can be purchased using the links above or at **RPVI.org** — simply click on "Events” + “St. Croix”

We look forward to seeing you there.

Regards,John Yob, RPVI Chairman

---

name: Carrie Anne
subject: One month to go! What is Forward doing, and how can you help?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Forward Party and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
Open me for party news you can use!

| | [ ](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=JgyyvCfQwldlSeD7KJl_Ih7269o_4hwqOhPs1_PHvgI&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_1&n=1)
---
| Hello Forward Friends- Wow. The past month was actually incredible. Forward has been doing the work, knocking on voters doors, attending the National Independents Convention, virtually introducing our candidates to you, and sending over **200k** texts in support of candidates. And that was only September! We still have one more month to go all in and get some Forwardists elected. But before I fill you in on all the upcoming opportunities, first I need to say a huge **THANK YOU** to everyone who attended our canvassing events in South Dakota and South Carolina! We can't accomplish any of this without you. Registering volunteers in SD Forward Friends meetup before canvassing in SC And if you missed last week's Meet the Forwadists, featuring independent Congressional candidates and hosted by **Andrew Yang** , click the button below to watch the recording! | [](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=kB45XuJbIaybua_uhXcc9p3GHOvxFcIOHqC8v0WARdbUct4xlcmSyZVXe8Is1OF7UROICcmVh7hu6RsqerV_Zjnzi90DCYS6gJVRBjqQSjc-qDNBqD1HAAMn_c5n4GoS&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_1&n=2 "Watch Meet the Forwardists Round 2") [Watch Meet the Forwardists Round 2](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=kB45XuJbIaybua_uhXcc9p3GHOvxFcIOHqC8v0WARdbUct4xlcmSyZVXe8Is1OF7UROICcmVh7hu6RsqerV_Zjnzi90DCYS6gJVRBjqQSjc-qDNBqD1HAAMn_c5n4GoS&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_1&n=2)
---
**_Forward March in Idaho_**
****Next up for Moving America Forward is Boise, Idaho! Volunteers will be canvassing over the weekend, leading up to a Town Hall on**Monday Oct 12th @ 5:30pm at Boise State** , moderated by Forward co-founder**Gov Chrisitine Todd Whitman.** They need volunteers to join them! Learn more[ here](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=hLf6ra6-T4Ek_sf_A8AjExyKRqRscbrf6yzmfvidBhx0S7-tA_uS0_cjGZOzO3d8&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_1&n=3).
There will also be a [Forward Friends meetup](https://home.forwardparty.com/id_forward_friends_meetup?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_1&n=4) **Sunday, Oct 11th at 6pm** \- if you or someone you know is in Boise, come hang with us!
**_Upcoming virtual events:_**
**Thurs Oct 1st & 8th @ 6:30pm ET- **[Forward Text Force](https://home.forwardparty.com/fwd_text_force_wk_1_20261001?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_1&n=5)
* Every Thurs until the election we will gather to onboard people to our text banking platform and send texts for our candidates together.

**TONIGHT Oct 1st @ 8pm ET** \- [Meet the Forwardists Round 3](meet.google.com/wtj-gdeb-ytu)
* Gov Whitman hosts the last round, featuring independent Senate and Gubernatorial candidates from various states.

**Tues Oct 13th @ 7:30pm ET** \- [National Volunteer Call](https://home.forwardparty.com/national_volunteer_call_20261013?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_1&n=6)
* Your first stop to getting involved with Forward. Includes party/candidate overview and how to use our website.

**Mon Oct 19th @ 6:30pm ET** \- [Welcome Team Training](https://home.forwardparty.com/welcome_team_intro_call_20261012?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_1&n=7)
* Want to help out on your own time? Learn how to call and welcome new Forward supporters in your state to our party.

I hope everyone is finding a way to play a part this election season. When we all work together we really can make a difference. Whether it's donating, canvassing, attending events, or sending texts at home from your phone, we all can all have an impact this year. Please reply to this email if you need help getting involved!
With hope and gratitude,
Carrie Anne
[https://home.forwardparty.com/](https://home.forwardparty.com/?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_1&n=8)

| Peter,
Eric Toney has my full support for Wisconsin Attorney General,**[and I ask you to join me by contributing to his campaign today.](https://link.action.erictoney.)**
In Congress, I have stood shoulder to shoulder with the men and women in uniform we rely on to enforce our laws and keep our communities safe. Eric Toney shares that commitment.
Since becoming Fond du Lac County District Attorney, Eric has put countless murderers, drug traffickers, and sexual assailants behind bars where they belong.
Compare Eric's record with what radical organizations supporting his opponent have in store if they get another four years of Josh Kaul as our AG.
The Democratic Socialists of America’s platform calls for **“fully abolishing the police and prison system.”** Freedom Inc. has declared its goal of defunding _the police department as we understand it—_ _**[“every single penny.”](https://link.action.erictoney.)**_
For me, the choice is clear. I trust and support tough-on-crime prosecutor Eric Toney as Wisconsin's next Attorney General, and **_[I encourage you to join me by contributing today.](https://link.action.erictoney.)_**
Sincerely,
**Congressman Bryan Steil

| | | | | | We apologize for any confusion caused by our email yesterday.There were originally two events planned with Speaker Mike Johnson on Tuesday: a fundraiser in Olympia and a rally in Chehalis. Speaker Johnson had an unavoidable travel delay, and we unfortunately only had time for one of the two events. His plane flew into Olympia, so it made the most sense for all involved to keep the Olympia fundraiser and postpone the Chehalis rally.

**Yesterday’s email was intended as a recap of the Olympia fundraiser. The rally will be held at a later date.** The good news is that Speaker Johnson is planning to return on October 21, and we plan to host another event for his upcoming visit. We’ll share additional details as soon as they are finalized.Thank you for your understanding, and again, we apologize for any confusion that was caused.Sincerely,

The foreign mining company getting the green light **just happens to be owned by a Chilean billionaire who provides a luxury residence to the President’s daughter.** It turns out the going rate for risking the most visited wilderness area in the United States is a nice rental property. You really can't make this stuff up. # Mansharamani Musings
---
| | [](https://us.list-manage.com/16lmN7Eexes?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)September was filled with noteworthy developments. The Fed raised rates, shattering hopes for the housing markets. AI safety grabbed global headlines. The United Nations met and successfully achieved....well, nothing. The Iran War continued, and diesel prices became front page news. Oh, and I almost forgot, government bond yields marched higher around the world.
See below for links to my thoughts about these (and other) topics as well as a speech I gave at the Freedom Summit are below...
Best wishes for a thought-provoking October!_**
- Vikram**_

[|

| | **SEPTEMBER 6, 2026**

The dream of almost every immigrant who arrives on our shores is that they will be measured not by their past or their parents’ professions but instead by their own ability. And more importantly, perhaps, that the next generation will grow up in a land of opportunity. Indeed, for generations, the goal of most parents (immigrant or not) was for their children to have it better than they did.
The path chosen to achieve this goal was almost always education. Many parents (mine included) prioritized education over almost every other activity. Time and money were dedicated to schooling and support for learning. And more often than not, the system worked. Many children of immigrant households found themselves entering elite schools and finding opportunities their parents never imagined.
I am living proof that it was possible for immigrants to come here, work hard, encourage and prioritize education for their children, and to see their children enjoy better lives. But this bargain rested on an assumption nobody really had to examine, at least not until today. We knew what that an education was valuable, distinguishing, and would retain its worth indefinitely. I am no longer confident in my last sentence...

| | **SEPTEMBER 13, 2026**

Every generation has a defining moment, one they carry with them for the rest of their lives. The one where time stops, the world changes, and all teens and adults remember where they were the moment they heard the news. These events tend to split time in a way that we thereafter demarcate life as before or after it. For our grandparents, it was Pearl Harbor. For our parents, the assassination of President John F. Kennedy. For our generation, it was the terrorist attacks of 9/11. And everyone remembers where they were.
For me, I was in Washington D.C. I was supposed to fly back to Boston on the morning of September 11, but my then-fiancée (and now wife), still at Harvard Law School, asked if I might be able to come back a bit early to help with some wedding planning. So I changed my flights and returned on Monday September 10th. I recall flying through a thunderstorm with jarring turbulence. And on 9/11, I was at my desk when I heard the news. Friends and family, who knew I was supposed to be flying, called to check on me.
And while in shock watching the news unfold on TV, I still remember being paralyzed with panic after learning that one of my friends had departed Logan to attend meetings in Los Angeles. A few hours later, his spouse and I shared a moment of sheer joy when we learned his boss, a very wealthy man, had insisted my friend connect...

| | **SEPTEMBER 20, 2026**

I run a frozen pizza factory in New Hampshire. We regularly have trucks pulling up to our loading dock with supplies such as flour, cheese, pepperoni, and packaging. And almost every day, trucks pull away carrying finished pizzas headed for stores across the country. Those trucks don’t run on gasoline. They run on diesel. And the average diesel price just hit [$6.43 a gallon](https://us.list-manage.com/10EwwyROeR2?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)...the highest price ever recorded in the United States.
That’s not just a number I read in a headline. It’s a number I see embedded on every invoice, every cost sheet, and every freight bill that crosses my desk. And that’s probably true for most manufacturers. Inputs arrive by trucks run on diesel. Outputs depart by trucks running on diesel. And it’s a number that is quietly raising the price of everything you buy...

| | **SEPTEMBER 27, 2026**

Regular readers of _Navigating Uncertainty_ know that I have long felt that global multilateral institutions such as the United Nations are ineffective and, in many cases, work against the interests of their member institutions. While the concept of global governance to coordinate global responses for global challenges makes intuitive sense, it simply hasn’t worked.

Global multilateralism has lost all credibility. Do we really think the UN Security Council is useful when one of its members is the aggressor in a war that’s killed millions? Or what about the World Health Organization, which refused to investigate the origins of COVID, the world’s biggest public health challenge in a century? Surely we can’t have faith in the World Trade Organization if it doesn’t address state-sponsored intellectual property theft?
