clean_body: A review of Vikram's September posts... | | | | | | | | | | | | | Mansharamani Musings | | was filled with noteworthy developments. The Fed raised rates, shattering hopes for the housing markets. AI safety grabbed global headlines. The United Nations met and successfully achieved....well, nothing. The Iran War continued, and diesel prices became front page news. Oh, and I almost forgot, government bond yields marched higher around the world. See below for links to my thoughts about these (and other) topics as well as a speech I gave at the Freedom Summit are below... Best wishes for a thought-provoking October! - Vikram | | SEPTEMBER 6, 2026 The dream of almost every immigrant who arrives on our shores is that they will be measured not by their past or their parents’ professions but instead by their own ability. And more importantly, perhaps, that the next generation will grow up in a land of opportunity. Indeed, for generations, the goal of most parents (immigrant or not) was for their children to have it better than they did. The path chosen to achieve this goal was almost always education. Many parents (mine included) prioritized education over almost every other activity. Time and money were dedicated to schooling and support for learning. And more often than not, the system worked. Many children of immigrant households found themselves entering elite schools and finding opportunities their parents never imagined. I am living proof that it was possible for immigrants to come here, work hard, encourage and prioritize education for their children, and to see their children enjoy better lives. But this bargain rested on an assumption nobody really had to examine, at least not until today. We knew what that an education was valuable, distinguishing, and would retain its worth indefinitely. I am no longer confident in my last sentence... | | | | SEPTEMBER 13, 2026 Every generation has a defining moment, one they carry with them for the rest of their lives. The one where time stops, the world changes, and all teens and adults remember where they were the moment they heard the news. These events tend to split time in a way that we thereafter demarcate life as before or after it. For our grandparents, it was Pearl Harbor. For our parents, the assassination of President John F. Kennedy. For our generation, it was the terrorist attacks of 9/11. And everyone remembers where they were. For me, I was in Washington D.C. I was supposed to fly back to Boston on the morning of September 11, but my then-fiancée (and now wife), still at Harvard Law School, asked if I might be able to come back a bit early to help with some wedding planning. So I changed my flights and returned on Monday September 10th. I recall flying through a thunderstorm with jarring turbulence. And on 9/11, I was at my desk when I heard the news. Friends and family, who knew I was supposed to be flying, called to check on me. And while in shock watching the news unfold on TV, I still remember being paralyzed with panic after learning that one of my friends had departed Logan to attend meetings in Los Angeles. A few hours later, his spouse and I shared a moment of sheer joy when we learned his boss, a very wealthy man, had insisted my friend connect... | | | | SEPTEMBER 20, 2026 I run a frozen pizza factory in New Hampshire. We regularly have trucks pulling up to our loading dock with supplies such as flour, cheese, pepperoni, and packaging. And almost every day, trucks pull away carrying finished pizzas headed for stores across the country. Those trucks don’t run on gasoline. They run on diesel. And the average diesel price just hit highest price ever recorded in the United States. That’s not just a number I read in a headline. It’s a number I see embedded on every invoice, every cost sheet, and every freight bill that crosses my desk. And that’s probably true for most manufacturers. Inputs arrive by trucks run on diesel. Outputs depart by trucks running on diesel. And it’s a number that is quietly raising the price of everything you buy... | | | | SEPTEMBER 27, 2026 Regular readers of Navigating Uncertainty know that I have long felt that global multilateral institutions such as the United Nations are ineffective and, in many cases, work against the interests of their member institutions. While the concept of global governance to coordinate global responses for global challenges makes intuitive sense, it simply hasn’t worked. Global multilateralism has lost all credibility. Do we really think the UN Security Council is useful when one of its members is the aggressor in a war that’s killed millions? Or what about the World Health Organization, which refused to investigate the origins of COVID, the world’s biggest public health challenge in a century? Surely we can’t have faith in the World Trade Organization if it doesn’t address state-sponsored intellectual property theft? Friend,
_**For 45 days, a 12-year-old girl lived through a nightmare no child should ever experience.** _ She had been trafficked, drugged, abused, and held against her will in a homeless encampment in California. **For 45 days, it seemed as if everyone had forsaken her.** **For 45 days, she suffered a living hell.** **For 45 days, she endured untold horrors.** [ _**Then came Day 46. That was the day our team at Heroes for Humanity went in and brought her out.** _ ](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=35eafdf3a028471ea6f341bc6ca62828&_e=tR4o9eSG0tbCWRi-N8YsnWWgeT4MIGtjpcg9IHofvzPiVIqxA794BN30CX_7-2r4Om-vQwyj3oDSJgNIGAUDFPjtgCXJfn2PV7ae88GnLNeM0NLMZ50Li7DUKlmuzfG5viIr0FC4PUjE_sMFjCdShFrsS8jiS8H24nHDbyqwP2irZBM2U44GLUWhVBDL-Y-GQX0y9yPAxWdszjpV4UMCnGWoHeQbSaoOF_AGyGiCM6llhuIFl9ftIFJTmtHSHv1-agkQK2dpeGKv1PRWsPaBsLUyF2ohdg0W5ug7Pjx358wCGS3p2FnwglBo7EkSR7FVyR7KZVmLa60wzJ8H-4kMvZiFQC6UGCEC8I5s2yRM3rRFq3AsnowjVDeTSTjqRucdNaNnzQaQZhkh7b79WdSF6TUJ0DhlodXyoGT5wdqUVgIVDFao5HNTPjoNXtVXYHBJeGWStq3K8jQ1mtJorUkkJY5PFZxNHZacWBSh2hBr50zlzxxAzuPJT3_YDgv_dNKpLfYe5aanJu7l-I8mPjzOmQ%3D%3D)
My name is Dennis Price, and I want to tell you why I'm sharing her story with you today. I believe God puts people in our path for a reason. Sometimes He calls us to pray. Sometimes He calls us to give. And sometimes He puts someone in front of us who desperately needs help, and then the Lord asks, “Who will go?” I have spent more than 19 years across various special operations units and private military contracting, and now I serve as a humanitarian and evangelist. I've seen suffering most people thankfully never will. I started Heroes for Humanity during the collapse in Afghanistan, watching Americans and vetted Afghan allies get hunted while the systems built to get them out failed completely. A small team and I helped rescue dozens of them. **That crucible proved how powerful it can be when good people refuse to look the other way.** We’ve carried that mission to all corners of the world, including responding to devastating earthquakes in Venezuela and Colombia this summer and the deadly Texas Hill Country floods last year. Our team is made up of veteran special operators, first responders, medical professionals, and everyday heroes who are willing to go into the places others can’t – or won’t – to rescue people in desperate need. [ _**For that little girl, it meant getting her out of an unimaginable situation and bringing her home.** _ ](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=35eafdf3a028471ea6f341bc6ca62828&_e=tR4o9eSG0tbCWRi-N8YsnWWgeT4MIGtjpcg9IHofvzPiVIqxA794BN30CX_7-2r4Om-vQwyj3oDSJgNIGAUDFPjtgCXJfn2PV7ae88GnLNeM0NLMZ50Li7DUKlmuzfG5viIr0FC4PUjE_sMFjCdShHAh0-ztZ0lqczPA1Y7p9qBMOplmx6lbpTn-MNf8HMgmVYdd7Ls_90UVMghoDwwo2kn7UXIBDHlP7KFD8ACogNh0SdJaTl5votdwCVJhwAD6ss4oYg8h18kpMyXWCgF6axzR6MT6c8BzZhGov7N55m-9fohp2ayxerU7adVnryrsg-D2LoBcUCXbXeCHEbkLL4aaelN72zv_aQcAVvPi3QfoYcNpJfdiNis56MuYr4RYL9HeDwK623yV3oiQqR3LfPrb0drVzathOWVYz-1m9W0FB9BkwBsdJp1v44qcCSqVBjFAasbtwa93-Z9yUDRzg0IBKURh62JlvVMNiQ_ASuefN7FcgWmhF5seb7goEZyI-g-01saLLVw6F8sjuy2liQ%3D%3D) In other cases, it could mean delivering lifesaving aid after a natural disaster, pulling families from a warzone, or simply being there on the worst day of someone’s life and reminding them that they have not been forgotten. But we can't wait until the next desperate call comes to get ready. Our operators have to be trained. Our equipment has to be ready. Vehicles need fuel. Medical supplies need to be stocked. Because when someone is waiting for their “Day 46,” every minute matters. **So, I’m asking you to do something today.** [ _**Will you make a gift of $10, $25, $50, or whatever you can afford to Heroes for Humanity?** _ ](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=35eafdf3a028471ea6f341bc6ca62828&_e=tR4o9eSG0tbCWRi-N8YsnWWgeT4MIGtjpcg9IHofvzPiVIqxA794BN30CX_7-2r4Om-vQwyj3oDSJgNIGAUDFPjtgCXJfn2PV7ae88GnLNeM0NLMZ50Li7DUKlmuzfG5viIr0FC4PUjE_sMFjCdShNRuJ5bLNDRUaFzQC4QZm6R63tg52zSwFmWxS2wlACvgr9_9zI3joO7yIZItJhMdJP3g24LIWAs3O6NWkSO1Op5US5yHlSng58R4gC2vo85my63HP9QguHwzsiqixZdBk9vlKYbzHFTQnRkq9LvdUsPrroMM7qIhAZjEXmS9BP_t6vgz6m31kK_uNZ-TVNtcT0_9ofnwNfKTBZ4ck6Cs92RiK5l8-STYd5SiEr02P97gOVdnDofIm_7LXsnECnoEqINbBary7gre3E5WzJclrlHZ1w9pVg1mCnK8RQsDd5nYDVVR622fRnAPrFSsEA0w_i8pdCGb9wu3Pl31xmKtR0uucPDeXpitNH_KNq4O4QlUZf2gI3DHJOzaT8Qjo4r79g%3D%3D) You may never be the person who physically walks into danger to bring someone home, but you can empower someone else to be that person. Your gift can be the hand that reaches across the world to comfort someone in need. [ _**And maybe, just maybe, God put this message in front of you today for a reason.** _ ](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=35eafdf3a028471ea6f341bc6ca62828&_e=tR4o9eSG0tbCWRi-N8YsnWWgeT4MIGtjpcg9IHofvzPiVIqxA794BN30CX_7-2r4Om-vQwyj3oDSJgNIGAUDFPjtgCXJfn2PV7ae88GnLNeM0NLMZ50Li7DUKlmuzfG5viIr0FC4PUjE_sMFjCdShLEoBYIWG_jWDCmgX4yyRkBfe3BjB74GjxUmDXG95VmvrGn1vYf4gTRC7q5MWS8ynaYFUI2xTSHs1HXAk2Eq3kYa0Av_32MkVMwiJKk-5dmJUSNGq4mAF34wQuLYmB_JNPnyJtrVucyEgAGBJt6dN-5dya0vI3yzqws8D2ZKn7aE4odiIVvzJFQLArxOpEfkJkJO-6XsFIxWhvZZNbJodtsIVIdoZp67dowM8nSaMi1vANyTERwOG9W7Cu5JWUfWbz7H50Er5sI-7TPDMRnBcLJzxHNAI-wro8DbEcMS_JWGe-UObt6S7j76a15-wlyL85yz5UXtCA7Ti88W4_LHVTJdsO9ZrGdtcst2skhaYeKcgb3L2hDB6y36q1-w3L0MXA%3D%3D)

# THE AARON DAY SHOW
Defending Free Will in the Age of Technocracy
S3E25 • Oct 1
## S3E25: Paxton's Baggage. Brown Is Ours. Texas Is the Senate. We're the Margin.
[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/GD60dr0wUuf?e=938a87a89b&c2id=c1b996ddd6cdaaf4cddb384f099ac837)
Aaron here.
On September 9, at the GOP's midterm convention in Dallas, Donald Trump mocked Ken Paxton's looks and the way he talks. Then he vowed to come back to Texas to elect him. My read: that is not loyalty. That is a man who needs the seat more than he respects the man running for it.
Back in May, Trump had endorsed Paxton as "a true MAGA Warrior." In 2023, Paxton's own Texas House impeached him 121 to 23. His own Senate acquitted him on every article. His office took over a case against Waco attorney Adam Dean Hoffman, charged with continuous sexual abuse of a child, and after a hung jury, offered a deal: plead guilty to two misdemeanors, one day in jail, no sex offender registration. The visiting judge, who previously served on the bench as a Republican, balked: "One day. Seriously?" Hoffman ended up serving twenty-nine days and surrendering his law license.
Paxton is the man Trump needs. Libertarian Ted Brown pulled 267,039 votes for U.S. Senate in 2024. Texas Southern's September poll already has him outpolling the Democrat among Libertarian Republicans. StarkFreedom backs Brown. We fund the margin. It costs the GOP the Senate.
The new episode, "The Puppet," airs tonight, Thursday, October 1, at 6:00 PM ET.

* **Stop corruption** by standing up to the special interests and political games that have made too many people lose faith in Washington.

name: Office of U.S. Senator Raphael Warnock
subject: Are you ready to vote?
body:
|
---
Neighbor,
As you may know, there is a federal election on **Tuesday, November 3rd** of this year. I believe that the right to vote is a foundational issue and that every eligible Georgian should be able to access the ballot box. I wanted to provide some information to help you prepare for election day. Even if you were registered to vote in the last election, it is strongly recommended that you check your registration.

Georgia's deadline to register to vote or change your voter registration is **Monday, October 5th**.

On the Georgia Secretary of State's My Voter Page ([https://mvp.sos.ga.gov/s/](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenWarnock&crop=16978.26559228.9347448.14245539&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fmvp.sos.ga.gov%2fs%2f&redir_log=084298489327169)), you can find a variety of tools and resources, including:

1. Check your voter registration status
2. Register to vote
3. Check your mail-in application and ballot status
4. Find poll locations
5. Find early voting locations
6. Find a list of your election officials
7. See a sample ballot for the upcoming election
8. Check your provisional ballot status
9. Check the voter identification requirements

On vote.gov ([https://vote.gov/](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenWarnock&crop=16978.26559228.9347448.14245539&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fvote.gov%2f&redir_log=526592696931117)), a federally run website, you can find voting guidance on a variety of topics, including:

1. Voting as a college student
2. Voting as a new U.S. citizen
3. Voting with a disability
4. Voting while unhoused
5. Voting after a felony conviction
6. Voting as a military service member
7. Voting as a U.S. citizen from outside the U.S.

As well as state-specific information. Additionally, if you have any specific questions or concerns with your ballot or voting, you can reach out to your local election officials. You can find their contact information here: [https://elections.sos.ga.gov/Elections/countyelectionoffices.do](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenWarnock&crop=16978.26559228.9347448.14245539&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2felections.sos.ga.gov%2fElections%2fcountyelectionoffices.do&redir_log=381504948176450). You can find more information on voter registration and casting your ballot on my Voter Resources webpage, here: [https://www.warnock.senate.gov/voting-resources/](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenWarnock&crop=16978.26559228.9347448.14245539&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.warnock.senate.gov%2fvoting-resources%2f&redir_log=252838814458341). The most powerful words uttered in our democracy are "the people have spoken." And I want to make sure that the people's voices are always heard on the floor of the United States Senate, in the Congress, and in the halls of power.

Please do not hesitate to contact me if I may be of assistance to you or your family.

Sincerely,

U.S. Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock

Friend, October is here, which means we’re just about one month away from Election Day! I wanted to take a break from our fundraising emails today to say **_thank you_**.
Thanks to your generosity and commitment to our mission, we officially hit our September end-of-quarter goal!
That is big news for our campaign. Hitting our goal means we’re well-positioned to keep pushing in these final 33 days. Your support helps us:
* **Keep our ads on the air** to spread our positive message and fight back against Roger Marshall’s attacks.
* **Travel across the state** to _listen_ to voters and learn what they want from their leaders.
* **Expand our team** so we can knock on doors and reach the undecided voters who will decide this election.
* **Keep our momentum going strong** so we can flip this seat in November!

Some folks see that it’s been 94 years since a Democrat won a Senate seat in Kansas and say it’s just impossible. **But together, we have built a movement that proves every day that change is possible. We really can make history here. **
**We simply could not have done it without you, friend.** So from me, LaVon and our whole team: _Thank you_.
Now let’s go win this thing!
— Adam

clean_body: We are almost one month away from Election Day. | | | = Friend, October is here, which means we’re just about one month away from Election Day! I wanted to take a break from our fundraising emails today to say thank you. Thanks to your generosity and commitment to our mission, we officially hit our September end-of-quarter goal! That is big news for our campaign. Hitting our goal means we’re well-positioned to keep pushing in these final 33 days. Your support helps us: Keep our ads on the air to spread our positive message and fight back against Roger Marshall’s attacks. Travel across the state to listen to voters and learn what they want from their leaders. Expand our team so we can knock on doors and reach the undecided voters who will decide this election. Keep our momentum going strong so we can flip this seat in November! Some folks see that it’s been 94 years since a Democrat won a Senate seat in Kansas and say it’s just impossible. But together, we have built a movement that proves every day that change is possible. We really can make history here. We simply could not have done it without you, friend. So from me, LaVon and our whole team: Thank you. Now let’s go win this thing! — Adam | | = | Adam Hamilton is a husband, father, pastor and fifth-generation Kansan. Now, he’s running for U.S. Senate as an independent-minded Democrat. Just like you, he’s tired of the chaos and corruption in Washington that is harming our farmers, raising costs at the checkout line and making critical health care services unattainable. He hears your concerns and is ready to get to work for you. Hi team,
**THANK YOU!**
**Because of your support, we hit our final end-of-quarter goal before the election.**
I'm really grateful that you've shown up for us time and time again.
**We launched this campaign one year ago today, and we 've built so much since then:**
* Outraising Dan in individual contributions
* Seeing our part of PA swing 33 points on average in the 2025 election
* Collecting 4,000 petition signatures to get on the ballot
* Hosting meet-and-greets and house parties all across the district
* Watching Josh Shapiro say this is the 5th flippable seat
* Going up on air with our first ad

We've built the momentum. And even Dan has noticed, which is why he is on air now calling me a socialist and trying to lie and buy his way into another term.
**The last year has been all about the next 33 days.**
We have big plans in October. Every dollar you contribute helps us make them even bigger and flip this seat in November.
**[Please chip in today to keep our grassroots campaign strong in the final stretch.](https://substack.com/redirect/67509087-f906-44c6-9877-d340d27d789b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Your support got us here, and it's going to be what gets us over the finish line.
Thank you for making everything we do possible.
Gratefully,
Rachel Wallace

| | Good Afternoon Team Demuth!
**Zoom Meeting**
I want to remind everyone that we will have our regularly scheduled grassroots volunteer meeting tonight at 8:30 PM. We will talk about yard signs, volunteer efforts, some events coming up, and much much more!
I have placed the link below. Once you click the link, you will be taken into a waiting room. I will let you into the meeting from there.
https://us06web.zoom.us/j/87316568944
**Update on Right Insight**
At 7:30 tonight, Caleb will be giving a separate training on Right Insight. This is a fantastic way to help out our campaign. **Even five minutes of phone calling, or door knocking even just your neighbors goes an incredibly long way!**
To join that meeting, please use the link below:

Virtual Right Insight Training
Thursday, October 1 · 7:30 – 8:15pm
Time zone: America/Chicago
Google Meet joining info
Video call link: [https://meet.google.com/ifb-fmzx-rkz](https://us.list-manage.com/SIFVBSWkY1o?e=422536b04e&c2id=3f96188058f7a1407b5cde0c924e7fd7)
Or dial: ‪(US) [+1 520-800-2262](tel:\(520\)%20800-2262)‬ PIN: ‪438 889 639‬#
More phone numbers: [https://tel.meet/ifb-fmzx-rkz?pin=2763407945023](https://us.list-manage.com/oHsiTSJdqPH?e=422536b04e&c2id=3f96188058f7a1407b5cde0c924e7fd7)
All of you that have previously been volunteers already have accounts. Simply download the app and sign in using the email address you received this message at. You will be sent a six-digit code to verify your identity, then you’re all logged in and ready to roll!For door knocking, we are utilizing a feature called Near Me. This will allow volunteers to go out and door knock houses that are nearby them. That list will change as you move around, so you can use it anywhere.Calls will be broken down by Congressional District. When we add you to Right Insight, we will assign you to calls specific for your area so you are talking to people who you may know, or share more common issues. Most of you will likely see all of them until we are able to organize you into Congressional district teams, so please just call into the CD you are from. For example, if you are from CD 1, call CD1.**If you do login and are told you do not have an account, please fill out the form below and we will get you added!**[ Sign up for a Right Insight Account.](https://us.list-manage.com/qJJTJppG8qP?e=422536b04e&c2id=3f96188058f7a1407b5cde0c924e7fd7)Both calls and door knocking projects are live and ready for volunteers. We are very excited to get everyone started! If you have technical questions or are unsure of how to get started, please call Caleb at 612-300-4202 or email him at Caleb@mngop.com**Signs** This meeting we will discuss our strategy for the final sign requests statewide and what we are doing to fill them. I will also update everyone on the call to our strategy regarding large signs.We look forward to seeing everyone on the call tonight! Thank you for joining us. With your help, we will elect Lisa Demuth as our next Governor and restore common sense to Minnesota.
---

Friend, Last night in Brentwood, **_something incredible happened._** **__** More than**400** fired-up supporters _packed the room_ , with folks spilling out into the hallways. **That’s what a movement looks like.** Thank you to everyone who showed up and proved that working families across Tennessee are _ready for real leadership._ While we were talking face-to-face with voters about the issues that actually matter— _good jobs, strong public schools, and keeping our communities healthy_ —**we had to ask the obvious question:_Where was Marsha?_** **__**_**Let’s be real**_ : last night, we were holding a packed event just ten minutes from her front door. If she wanted to talk to everyday Tennesseans, she could have walked right over. Instead, she’s missing in action. _**And it's a pattern.**_ Fresh off filing a federal lawsuit in Tennessee against former Special Counsel Jack Smith over her phone records, Marsha somehow found it convenient to skip the very high-stakes congressional hearing where Smith testified. She’s more than happy to launch legal attacks from a safe distance, but when it’s time to answer to the public, _she consistently ducks out._ When a politician dodges accountability, whether it's avoiding her own constituents ten minutes away or skipping out on legislative hearings,_it raises an obvious question:_**_What is she trying to hide?_****** **__** We aren't waiting around for politicians who won't show up for the people they claim to represent. **We've got another empty podium debate coming up this weekend,_and we want you there with us._** **Join us this Saturday in Nashville for our next big Town Hall:**
* **When:** This Saturday, October 3 at 2:30 PM CDT
* **Where:** White Hall — 1034 W Kirkland Ave, Nashville, TN 37216
* **Special Guest:** _State Senator Charlane Oliver_
* **Moderator:** Content creator and changemaker,_Monte Mader_

That’s what a movement looks like. Thank you to everyone who showed up and proved that working families across Tennessee are ready for real leadership. While we were talking face-to-face with voters about the issues that actually matter— good jobs, strong public schools, and keeping our communities healthy —we had to ask the obvious question:Where was Marsha? _Let’s be real : last night, we were holding a packed event just ten minutes from her front door. If she wanted to talk to everyday Tennesseans, she could have walked right over. Instead, she’s missing in action. And it's a pattern. Fresh off filing a federal lawsuit in Tennessee against former Special Counsel Jack Smith over her phone records, Marsha somehow found it convenient to skip the very high-stakes congressional hearing where Smith testified. She’s more than happy to launch legal attacks from a safe distance, but when it’s time to answer to the public, she consistently ducks out. Attorney Ralph Lorigo told a Senate roundtable what he watched hospital administrators do to dying patients. Five years later, no one has answered for it in a criminal courtroom. A conversation with a federal prosecutor gave me the nerve to ask why.
On Monday, September 28, Senator Ron Johnson convened a roundtable titled "COVID-19 Hospital Protocols: Real Stories from Real People." Among the witnesses was Ralph Lorigo -- a Buffalo attorney, Erie County Conservative Party chairman -- whose firm sued hospitals across some forty states for refusing to give ivermectin to dying COVID patients, including one that defied a judge's order to administer it. Two days later, the true-crime author John Leake published an essay that says out loud what Lorigo's case files have implied for half a decade: the administrators who said no should be tried for murder, or at least negligent homicide. Leake invited readers to tell him he's exaggerating. I'm declining...

**Hey****,**
I have to be honest, we have 5 days until early voting starts in Ohio, and I don’t want to sugarcoat how things look right now.
When Fairshake, a crypto-backed super PAC, announced it was spending $30 million on this campaign, we saw overwhelming support from everyday people who stand against the over $250 million in Republican spending I’m now up against.
But since then, **our fundraising has hit a deep slump** , and in the next few days we may have to make budget cuts – while dark-money groups get to spend millions a day in Ohio. _Combined Republican groups are outspending us 7:1 every day right now._
We know that not everyone can chip in – and we don’t expect folks to donate to every email we send out, but with enough support we can get through the finish line and come out strong in November.
**[Will you please chip in $5 to my campaign today? This fundraising slump is coming at the worst possible time, and we have to close the gap between my campaign and the special interest groups spending in Ohio.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140456553/650548763/-1024831887?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=email_fr_gmailnd_jtk6474&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmY2IzYzk3Ny1lM2JkLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LDEQWSQ_C7Z2UTjqgA2XVYELX63tMS2ZZVFQ7rY2rok=)**
| | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140456554/650548765/-1024831887?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=email_fr_gmailnd_jtk6474&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmY2IzYzk3Ny1lM2JkLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LDEQWSQ_C7Z2UTjqgA2XVYELX63tMS2ZZVFQ7rY2rok=)

This race is in a dead heat, and Republicans know the spending they are pouring in will move the needle in their direction, and we can’t afford to let that happen. The latest ad blitz has brought this race into a statistical tie, and a poll released last week by Quantum Polling has us 47-47 against my opponent.
Every election expert has said the same thing – that this race is anyone’s game. We’re one of two races consistently ranked a “toss-up” by every major race rater. That’s not an accident.
We’re just 33 days away from the election, and need to hit every fundraising goal between now and then. If we show any signs of weakness, National Republicans will jump at the opportunity to keep spending hundreds of millions in Ohio. name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: My bill on AI safety ➡️
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
AI is developing at a reckless, alarming rate — and working people are paying the price.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20261001-6788-footer&t=1&akid=6788%2E420207%2E2oa2Ev)
Peter,
People keep asking: When is Congress finally going to do something about AI? The conversation around the catastrophic risks of AI is getting louder and louder – and we have been too slow to act.
**I refuse to wait any longer. Today I’m releasing my framework for a National AI Charter Act.**
This framework is a comprehensive solution aimed at reigning in these powerful AI companies.
A national charter forces companies to meet strict public interest, safety, and spinoff requirements. In doing so, the charter breaks Big Tech’s grip on AI and ensures dangerous AI models are not developed or released.
**We must act because the dangers of unchecked AI development are no longer hypothetical. They’re showing up in people’s lives right now.**
Recently, I heard from a mother who lost her son after receiving dangerous, false medical information from a chatbot, instead of being connected to a professional who could actually help him.
Her story is devastating, and preventable.
**No one should lose their life because a greedy corporation decided to move too fast and worry about the consequences later.**
Workers across the country are being forced to train AI systems that will replace their own jobs. Engineers and developers inside these companies are sounding the alarm at how recklessly this technology is being developed. And the American people are demanding action as data centers encroach into our communities.
Workers whose livelihoods are being eliminated. Families who are grieving. Communities whose water and energy are being drained to power data centers they never asked for.
**Peter, let me be clear about what we’re up against: groups associated with OpenAI and Anthropic have poured over $56 million into the midterms this cycle.**
These corporations are not just developing AI too quickly with zero regard for the human cost — they’re buying the politicians who are supposed to regulate them. Working people _need_ to be in the driver’s seat of this technology. Not crushed underneath it.
Congress is facing a crossroads: treat the AI industry as too big to question, or regulate it and require it to serve the public.
I choose the latter, every single time. This moment is urgent, and we must meet it.
**That’s why I’m proposing a National AI Charter that requires AI companies to operate on the public’s terms or not at all. We need round-the-clock government oversight to keep the public safe from risky AI. We need to break Big Tech’s grip on AI. And we need serious criminal consequences for the billionaires driving AI’s race to the bottom.**
I’m going to fight for major regulations to hold AI companies accountable and put real, enforceable safeguards in place before irreparable damage is done. [**If you’re able, will you please make a $3 contribution today to help keep me in Congress fighting for AI safety?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261001-1.pGXDTp&refcode=em20261001-6788&amount=3&t=2&akid=6788%2E420207%2E2oa2Ev)

In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

Peter, does $1,050,000,000 mean anything to you? That $1.05 billion (billion with a B!) is the staggering amount of money that billionaires like Elon Musk have poured into the coffers of Republican candidates this year. Republicans are desperate and terrified of losing power. First, they **egregiously gerrymandered maps to try to rig the outcome.** Then, they **pushed voter suppression policies** to make it harder for the average citizen to vote. **And now they're asking their billionaire friends to throw money at their problem.** Here’s the thing: It’s hard to compete with a billion dollars — especially in the critical state-level races where budgets are typically smaller. One massive check could drown out a campaign’s message. **Look, we can’t beat them at their own game, so we need to band together to out-organize them — over the next 40 days, the NDRC is working to elect Democracy Defenders in more than 300 critical races across the country.[Donate today to build grassroots support and ensure that we, the people — not the money of MAGA billionaires — determine the outcome of this election.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140457216/650550724/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_1.05Billion_email_20261001-NDRC-Tier1-1.05Billion_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20261001-NDRC-Tier1-1.05Billion_&utm_campaign=1.05Billion&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjFlZWFkN2RmLWU0YmQtZjExMS1hNmE5LTAwMGQzYTU2ZDJmNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=L4fZCxkrtNYMKxcULHtyUfJgN9B1qu9gtqQm5NI611k=)** The fact is: If the Republican strategy succeeds, losing the midterms won’t just show that the system is broken. It might prevent us from getting the chance to fix it. That’s why we’ve insisted on investing in an ambitious slate of state-level races that we believe will have the most sway over the fight for fair elections and a stronger democracy. It’s frankly offensive to the idea of democracy that the wealthiest people on Earth think they can just purchase their preferred electoral outcome. That’s why we all need to step up for the final push of this election. [**Make a gift to elect pro-democracy candidates and help us weather these attacks on fairness — whether they come from power-hungry lawmakers or cynical billionaires. Three national polls in twelve days read like a failed stress test. Quinnipiac, out this morning: Democrats 51, Republicans 39 on the House ballot, with independents going 54-30 for the Democrats. Emerson, September 24: 53-42, independents +29 Democratic. NPR/PBS/Marist, September 15: 53-41, independents +25. Eleven- and twelve-point margins with the middle gone. That's not a midterm breeze. That's a structural event -- and the structure is this: for the first time in a generation, the Republican establishment is being outflanked from its own right, by its own voters, in its own counties, on its own issues.
Four fronts tell the story.
**One** : data centers. Marist finds Republicans are the only group with a majority -- 54 percent -- calling AI data centers good for the country. Then the question turns local, and the pattern reverses. A Fox poll puts opposition to a data center in their area at 60 percent among Republicans, including 53 percent of MAGA voters. UMass finds 11 percent national support for one in your community. Ohio backs a construction ban 71 percent. POLITICO watched nearby-opposition jump from 28 to 41 percent in six months. So Republican county commissions -- like Buchanan County, Iowa, where GOP supervisor Dawn Vogel voted for a moratorium and says she hasn't met one voter who wants a server farm -- are doing the vetoing the White House won't: 75 projects worth roughly $130 billion blocked in one quarter, 375 bills in statehouses this year, a record. Trump's answer is to call resisting communities "backwards and poor." His endorsed Florida gubernatorial nominee -- "Data Center Donalds" -- is tied or trailing a Democrat running on a moratorium; Paxton and Talarico are deadlocked in Texas; the DCCC is salivating over 24 GOP districts in Ohio and Michigan. And today's Quinnipiac delivers the verdict line: _71 percent_ of voters prefer candidates who support stricter AI guardrails.
**Two** : Flock cameras. Overton Insights polls Texas likely voters and finds 63.6 percent oppose license-plate readers at public intersections. This is not an Austin thing. College Station's police logged 763,148 unique plates in one month. Officers have been accused of abusing the data in Baytown, Katy, Pasadena, and Fort Bend County; Lufkin's chief suspended the program after an officer was arraigned. Politico's dispatch on the backlash -- "work boots and Subarus" -- is the tell: the revolt is bipartisan, and heavy on the boots. A state senator is now demanding "Get the Flock out of Texas." The party of leave-me-alone signed multiyear contracts to log every plate on every farm road, and the base is rising up at the commissioners' court -- where the contracts are actually signed.
**Three** : the trans issue. Pew, August 11: 56 percent of Americans are "not at all comfortable" with transgender athletes on teams that don't match their birth sex; 66 percent favor laws requiring competition by birth sex; an NYT poll found nearly 80 percent opposition. This is the single most popular plank in the 2024 Republican platform -- a three-quarters issue. And a unified Republican government let it die, 51-45, on a March 2025 cloture vote, and never made it a priority again. No floor week. No reconciliation vehicle. Nothing. When you own a 70-30 issue and budget nothing to enact it, your voters eventually conclude you were performing.
Too little too late? The federal bill aimed at reshaping the college sports industry took a major step toward becoming law Monday night when the U.S. Senate overwhelmingly voted 77-22 to pass it. As NCAA president Charlie Baker said in a statement Monday night, "Student-athletes from across the country and all three NCAA Divisions worked hard to get this legislation moving and thanks to their advocacy, the bill just received a massive, bipartisan vote in the Senate.
"Now the bill moves to the U.S. House of Representatives _and there is much work left to do to_ ensure student-athlete benefits are codified into federal law and future generations of young people can access those benefits and use college sports as the launching point for their careers." Too cute with 5 weeks until election.
**Four** : immigration. Reuters/Ipsos this month: Trump's approval on illegal immigration has fallen to 39 percent, a new low, with 58 percent saying the crackdown goes too far -- after federal agents fatally shot two U.S. citizens during protest confrontations. AP-NORC found the same majority sentiment in July. Establishment Republicans will read that as the base wants less enforcement. Wrong. It says the enforcement reads as theater instead of law -- Home Depot raids and protest skirmishes -- while the structural conservative items rot. Senator Hagerty's bill to put a citizenship question on the 2030 census and apportion seats to citizens has sat Introduced in committee for fifteen months, with 18 Republican co-sponsors and no hearing. The unaccompanied-minor pipeline that released some 700,000 children into the interior -- 233,000 of whom were never served court papers -- kept running; the proof arrived in Talladega last Friday, when a federal judge sentenced a Guatemalan reentering under a fake name to 31 months. Losing the middle and the right simultaneously isn't governing conservatively. It's governing for the tribute videos. Remember birthright citizenship law passed by SCOTUS?
The pattern. Notice what Democrats did to win: nothing. They didn't win these voters; they showed up where the GOP wasn't -- with a moratorium, a repeal, a bill. Every one of these fights is a _county_ fight -- a courthouse vote, a school board, a sheriff's contract -- and in every one, the GOP's own officeholders stand on the other side of their own electorate, shielded by vendors, utilities, and an endorsement machine that has spent nine years picking the establishment horse: Strange, Romney, Loeffler, Oz, Vance, McCormick, Sheehy, now Donalds.
The Whigs didn't die in a general election. They died at the county level, in about two years, when the activists who did the party's work concluded it was being managed for other people's interests -- and walked. Five weeks out, the GOP is running that experiment again, with worse numbers: 63.6 percent of Texans against the cameras, 60 percent of its own voters against the servers, three-quarters against the schools, 39 percent on the issue it sold everything to own. If the wave comes on November 3, don't look for it at the edge of the blue states. Look for the clipboard outside the county courthouse -- and read the party affiliation of the people holding it.
I didn't even mention price of diesel and too much government in health care...look out below.

It's forming on the Republican right flank -- in red counties, on red issues. | | | Oct 1 | | | | | | | | | | | | Three national polls in twelve days read like a failed stress test. Quinnipiac, out this morning: Democrats 51, Republicans 39 on the House ballot, with independents going 54-30 for the Democrats. Emerson, September 24: 53-42, independents +29 Democratic. NPR/PBS/Marist, September 15: 53-41, independents +25. Eleven- and twelve-point margins with the middle gone. That's not a midterm breeze. That's a structural event -- and the structure is this: for the first time in a generation, the Republican establishment is being outflanked from its own right, by its own voters, in its own counties, on its own issues. Four fronts tell the story. One : data centers. Marist finds Republicans are the only group with a majority -- 54 percent -- calling AI data centers good for the country. Then the question turns local, and the pattern reverses. A Fox poll puts opposition to a data center in their area at 60 percent among Republicans, including 53 percent of MAGA voters. UMass finds 11 percent national support for one in your community. Ohio backs a construction ban 71 percent. POLITICO watched nearby-opposition jump from 28 to 41 percent in six months. So Republican county commissions -- like Buchanan County, Iowa, where GOP supervisor Dawn Vogel voted for a moratorium and says she hasn't met one voter who wants a server farm -- are doing the vetoing the White House won't: 75 projects worth roughly $130 billion blocked in one quarter, 375 bills in statehouses this year, a record. Trump's answer is to call resisting communities "backwards and poor." His endorsed Florida gubernatorial nominee -- "Data Center Donalds" -- is tied or trailing a Democrat running on a moratorium; Paxton and Talarico are deadlocked in Texas; the DCCC is salivating over 24 GOP districts in Ohio and Michigan. And today's Quinnipiac delivers the verdict line: 71 percent of voters prefer candidates who support stricter AI guardrails. Two : Flock cameras. Overton Insights polls Texas likely voters and finds 63.6 percent oppose license-plate readers at public intersections. This is not an Austin thing. College Station's police logged 763,148 unique plates in one month. Officers have been accused of abusing the data in Baytown, Katy, Pasadena, and Fort Bend County; Lufkin's chief suspended the program after an officer was arraigned. Politico's dispatch on the backlash -- "work boots and Subarus" -- is the tell: the revolt is bipartisan, and heavy on the boots. A state senator is now demanding "Get the Flock out of Texas." The party of leave-me-alone signed multiyear contracts to log every plate on every farm road, and the base is rising up at the commissioners' court -- where the contracts are actually signed. Three : the trans issue. Pew, August 11: 56 percent of Americans are "not at all comfortable" with transgender athletes on teams that don't match their birth sex; 66 percent favor laws requiring competition by birth sex; an NYT poll found nearly 80 percent opposition. This is the single most popular plank in the 2024 Republican platform -- a three-quarters issue. And a unified Republican government let it die, 51-45, on a March 2025 cloture vote, and never made it a priority again. No floor week. No reconciliation vehicle. Nothing. When you own a 70-30 issue and budget nothing to enact it, your voters eventually conclude you were performing. Too little too late? The federal bill aimed at reshaping the college sports industry took a major step toward becoming law Monday night when the U.S. Senate overwhelmingly voted 77-22 to pass it. As NCAA president Charlie Baker said in a statement Monday night, "Student-athletes from across the country and all three NCAA Divisions worked hard to get this legislation moving and thanks to their advocacy, the bill just received a massive, bipartisan vote in the Senate. "Now the bill moves to the U.S. House of Representatives and there is much work left to do to ensure student-athlete benefits are codified into federal law and future generations of young people can access those benefits and use college sports as the launching point for their careers." Too cute with 5 weeks until election. Four : immigration. Reuters/Ipsos this month: Trump's approval on illegal immigration has fallen to 39 percent, a new low, with 58 percent saying the crackdown goes too far -- after federal agents fatally shot two U.S. citizens during protest confrontations. AP-NORC found the same majority sentiment in July. Establishment Republicans will read that as the base wants less enforcement. Wrong. It says the enforcement reads as theater instead of law -- Home Depot raids and protest skirmishes -- while the structural conservative items rot. Senator Hagerty's bill to put a citizenship question on the 2030 census and apportion seats to citizens has sat Introduced in committee for fifteen months, with 18 Republican co-sponsors and no hearing. The unaccompanied-minor pipeline that released some 700,000 children into the interior -- 233,000 of whom were never served court papers -- kept running; the proof arrived in Talladega last Friday, when a federal judge sentenced a Guatemalan reentering under a fake name to 31 months. Losing the middle and the right simultaneously isn't governing conservatively. It's governing for the tribute videos. Remember birthright citizenship law passed by SCOTUS? The pattern. Notice what Democrats did to win: nothing. They didn't win these voters; they showed up where the GOP wasn't -- with a moratorium, a repeal, a bill. Every one of these fights is a county fight -- a courthouse vote, a school board, a sheriff's contract -- and in every one, the GOP's own officeholders stand on the other side of their own electorate, shielded by vendors, utilities, and an endorsement machine that has spent nine years picking the establishment horse: Strange, Romney, Loeffler, Oz, Vance, McCormick, Sheehy, now Donalds. The Whigs didn't die in a general election. They died at the county level, in about two years, when the activists who did the party's work concluded it was being managed for other people's interests -- and walked. Five weeks out, the GOP is running that experiment again, with worse numbers: 63.6 percent of Texans against the cameras, 60 percent of its own voters against the servers, three-quarters against the schools, 39 percent on the issue it sold everything to own. If the wave comes on November 3, don't look for it at the edge of the blue states. Look for the clipboard outside the county courthouse -- and read the party affiliation of the people holding it. I didn't even mention price of diesel and too much government in health care...look out below. Thanks for reading! This post is public so feel free to share it. name: Kailee for Congress
subject: Official invitation for Peter
body:
I want you beside me as we build this campaign from the ground up.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/fNy03Vwttrt?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Peter, I wanted to personally thank you for joining our campaign.
I grew up in Auburn in a blue-collar family. My dad spent 41 years working as a correctional officer. My mom is a nurse who cares for Alzheimer’s patients. I worked multiple jobs to put myself through school, became the first person in my family to earn a four-year degree, and spent years paying off my student loans.

Friend, Happy October 1st! Rachel launched her campaign ONE YEAR ago today — and now, we’re counting on your help to get us through to November 3rd! Let’s finish strong. Scroll down for the latest from the trail and find out how you can pitch in for the final stretch! **Ways To Get Involved This Week**
1. 👀**We have brand new ads dropping across digital platforms Tuesday!** Keep an eye out for them, and share with your networks if you see them on your Facebook page. Check out a sneak peek below!
2. Our town hall series starts **NEXT WEEK** with a kickoff in Annville on Tuesday, followed by Shartlesville on Wednesday. You can find all the details [on our website](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140458217/650553909/-295247600?refcode=b26_em_msg_2026.10.01_b1_ktwfc_newsletter&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjA5NjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNGZhNDg2MTEtZThiZC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=gO9Un5O9jxQgliibUNDOvNK7mXUdfriQngah-jJWcQE=&emci=47fc5a6f-c2bd-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=4fa48611-e8bd-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=18681717) — make sure you share with your friends, and we’ll see you out there!
3. **Sign up to canvass in your community!** We are hitting the pavement nearly every day around the district to get out the word about Rachel. Reach out to John ([john@wallaceforcongress.com](mailto:john@wallaceforcongress.com)) to get what you need to knock doors.
4. [Join our next phone bank!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140458218/650553910/-535849788?occurrenceId=&source=f43fb13a-b510-44c6-bc5e-bf53f8b15611&refcode=b26_em_msg_2026.10.01_b1_ktwfc_newsletter&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjA5NjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNGZhNDg2MTEtZThiZC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=gO9Un5O9jxQgliibUNDOvNK7mXUdfriQngah-jJWcQE=&emci=47fc5a6f-c2bd-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=4fa48611-e8bd-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=18681717) Whether you come to our office in Pottsville or you choose to make calls from your couch, we need your help calling voters to make sure they have a plan to vote. Three states are about to decide a lot more than 2026.

| | | |
---
Fellow Patriot,
---
We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let me explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.

Peter, As we look ahead to the cases the Supreme Court will consider next, one thing is clear: the Court’s decisions will have a huge impact on our collective safety and daily lives. But these cases will be heard by a Supreme Court that has been bought and directed by MAGA special interests, not one that can be trusted to uphold our Constitution. **[Right now, our partners are preparing for the work ahead as we fight to hold this Court accountable to the people, not special interests. Can you fund our fight?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsQNarR6PCR1lUtXpWTyhe65fajRKP7aRkqZUbctKBS3Sez_cs19IHD6c7AHnvqOOCmTeC5D-1gs8QZ0323yMEMR3LgkWCRVlyafSeMahZe1YY9pDzaxYwO_jTVyyTgiAB0zPyAXZpdvy6HxeUaSRSpvSOTor4Tc61tyKdu-xDDW4u0daimdPiB63nLWMky2hCxewWdqe7v47OE7nl5uAkupYzqP6_GxL5oyep2PuUYPYPX0tbR1cNk4VT7O4mg5Wj2Lr70MOPjSI6PKQAAzDHorfNrG45E1dkQWRxC2WhhcNCHSN1ILMiqR4tmo5q4RbQ/4ui/c5DFJ5f3T7mTaXUGcp5FvA/h0/h001.B5rzOOoE48-_7f9HB3pX_YEP_-3OhklRgRsNkn6Zr5k)** This term, the Court will consider assault weapon bans in Connecticut and Illinois and rule on whether the Second Amendment guarantees the right to carry assault weapons.1 Earlier this year, in case that is still pending, a federal appeals court struck down New Jersey’s longstanding ban on assault weapons on Second Amendment grounds–the first decision of its kind.2 **Freedom is being able to go to school, worship, gather, shop, work,****_and live_****without fearing a spree shooter will end your life, but if the Supreme Court rules that assault weapons bans are unconstitutional, our families and communities will be at risk.** The Court will also consider two cases on LGBTQ+ rights, again with high stakes in the real world. In Colorado, The Catholic Archdiocese of Denver is challenging the state’s Universal Preschool Program after being excluded after refusing to sign a nondiscrimination agreement covering “sexual orientation” and “gender identity.” A SCOTUS ruling in favor of the Archdiocese could allow organizations with religious objections to refuse to serve LGBTQ+ people without repercussions.3 In Washington state, parents are challenging laws that allow youth shelters to provide services, including gender affirming care, to minors without notifying their parents. This case could open the door for parents and anti-trans groups to sue shelters or medical practitioners providing essential care for transgender youth.4 **We’ve already seen how a captured Court’s decisions play out in the real world, and it’s not good.** After the Court upheld state laws banning transgender girls and women from school sports teams, House Republicans advanced a bill that would define “sex” under Title IX as only biologically determined male or female. And New Jersey’s assault weapons ban only came under fire _after_ the Supreme Court’s 2022 landmark decision on gun rights changed how judges consider those cases. **Peter, this is how they shrink our rights one step at a time. clean_body: | | Peter, As we look ahead to the cases the Supreme Court will consider next, one thing is clear: the Court’s decisions will have a huge impact on our collective safety and daily lives. But these cases will be heard by a Supreme Court that has been bought and directed by MAGA special interests, not one that can be trusted to uphold our Constitution. This term, the Court will consider assault weapon bans in Connecticut and Illinois and rule on whether the Second Amendment guarantees the right to carry assault weapons.1 Earlier this year, in case that is still pending, a federal appeals court struck down New Jersey’s longstanding ban on assault weapons on Second Amendment grounds–the first decision of its kind.2 Freedom is being able to go to school, worship, gather, shop, work,and livewithout fearing a spree shooter will end your life, but if the Supreme Court rules that assault weapons bans are unconstitutional, our families and communities will be at risk. The Court will also consider two cases on LGBTQ+ rights, again with high stakes in the real world. In Colorado, The Catholic Archdiocese of Denver is challenging the state’s Universal Preschool Program after being excluded after refusing to sign a nondiscrimination agreement covering “sexual orientation” and “gender identity.” A SCOTUS ruling in favor of the Archdiocese could allow organizations with religious objections to refuse to serve LGBTQ+ people without repercussions.3 In Washington state, parents are challenging laws that allow youth shelters to provide services, including gender affirming care, to minors without notifying their parents. This case could open the door for parents and anti-trans groups to sue shelters or medical practitioners providing essential care for transgender youth.4 We’ve already seen how a captured Court’s decisions play out in the real world, and it’s not good. After the Court upheld state laws banning transgender girls and women from school sports teams, House Republicans advanced a bill that would define “sex” under Title IX as only biologically determined male or female. And New Jersey’s assault weapons ban only came under fire after the Supreme Court’s 2022 landmark decision on gun rights changed how judges consider those cases. Peter, this is how they shrink our rights one step at a time. A decision from the captured Court decision justifies new legislation or rulings, which become the basis for more legal challenges, tightening the screws until everyday, working people are left fighting a system built against them. The American people are not powerless. But we need to build demand so big that Congress cannot keep treating this captured Court like business as usual. That is why United for Democracy is fighting to reform the Court, repair our democracy, and build a system that answers to working people, not dark money donors. clean_body: New Jersey deserves answers| | | | | Friend: I wanted to be sure you saw the news: I am suing Mikie Sherrill for failing to release the records of the over 6,600 illegal aliens in New Jersey who were registered to vote, 400 of whom cast votes in our elections. | | | | Months ago, I asked for the records showing how New Jersey maintains its voter rolls. Those records have not been released. I will not accept unanswered questions about the integrity of our elections. So, I am taking this fight to court. New Jerseyans deserve to know how this happened, what has been done to correct the rolls, and how officials will keep it from happening again. Peter , This month, I’m heading to four college campuses across the country to talk with students about the future of our nation. Young people have a lot at stake in the decisions being made today, from the cost of living and access to good jobs to technology, war and peace, and the future of our democracy. I want to hear about what’s going right, what’s not working, and what’s on people’s minds.**And I want to see you there.**

clean_body: Young people deserve to be heard, so I’m taking the conversation directly to campus.| | | | Peter , This month, I’m heading to four college campuses across the country to talk with students about the future of our nation. Young people have a lot at stake in the decisions being made today, from the cost of living and access to good jobs to technology, war and peace, and the future of our democracy. I want to hear about what’s going right, what’s not working, and what’s on people’s minds.And I want to see you there. Here’s where you can find me, with links to RSVP for each event. These events are free and open to the public, but space is limited—make sure you secure your spot today! October 19 — Boston, MA October 20 — Orlando, FL with Congressman Maxwell Frost, Angie Nixon, and Rep. Anna Eskamani October 21 — Berkeley, CA with Jane Kim October 22 — Ann Arbor, MI Every time we show up somewhere, we have an opportunity to build this movement from the ground up. That’s what this tour is about: meeting people on their own turf and learning directly from them. That’s the way we build a movement people are excited to be a part of. But traveling, putting on events, creating spaces for people to have a dialogue, and bringing the teams together to make it happen—it all costs real money. = = = Young people have every reason to be frustrated with our politics. The least we can do is show up and listen. If we’re serious about building a country that works for the next generation, we need to hear what they have to say today. name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: Why I am feeling hopeful
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
I just got home from a few days organizing in Buffalo, Ithaca, and Syracuse, and I have to tell you I’m coming back feeling pretty hopeful.
I went to these places to launch an organizing program across New York. Over these next 5 weeks, organizers and volunteers will be knocking on doors and canvassing with the specific goal of reaching people who have not voted in two consecutive federal elections and are at risk of being purged from the voter rolls.
Launching this program and speaking with organizers has filled me with hope that the energy to elect Democrats up and down the ballot is out there if we can channel it into turning people out who may have previously felt left behind or that their vote did not matter.
The way we do that is by giving people something worth showing up for: Medicare for All, universal childcare, a living wage, and a government that actually works for them.
Oligarchs who profit from division want working people afraid of each other. But what I saw upstate — people enjoying the Ithaca Apple Festival, connecting in Churches, students asking questions at a town hall — is what happens when people stop being afraid of their neighbors and start organizing with them instead.
Solidarity is contagious.
_The Ithaca Apple Festival_
_Training organizers how to do effective voter outreach_

_Listening to college students in Ithaca and taking their questions_
If we can get people excited to vote in Buffalo, Ithaca, and Syracuse, we can build it across the nation in 2026, 2028 and beyond, because organizing does not start and end in the weeks around an election. Thank you for being a part of this campaign.
Whether you made a donation, signed up for a volunteer shift, or talked to a neighbor, you are part of how we build this together.
With your support, I'm going to spend every one of these next 33 days fighting to take back the House and Senate, and to give every working person a reason to vote on November 3rd.
In solidarity,
Alexandria

And for 30 years, Susan Collins has failed us. Time and again, she has sold us out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. And I’m sick of it.

Let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me.

When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us.

After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that nothing would change unless there were working-class voices in power.

So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people.

I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.

I’m building this campaign the right way. With grassroots support from folks like you. I’m not running to impress the billionaires or the corporate class. I’m running for the mom who’s worried about how she’ll fill her gas tank this week. I’m running for the kid whose whole life will be determined by the quality of his education. I’m running to ensure every working family in Maine has the government they deserve.

After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that nothing would change unless there were working-class voices in power. So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people. I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family. I’m building this campaign the right way. With grassroots support from folks like you. I’m not running to impress the billionaires or the corporate class. I’m running for the mom who’s worried about how she’ll fill her gas tank this week. I’m running for the kid whose whole life will be determined by the quality of his education.
